# Indostates Health — EMR Module Atlas & UI Mockup Brief

A complete module, screen and workflow specification for the Indostates Health
hospital EMR platform, written to be read front-to-back by a designer and turned
into UI mockups without further questions. **28 modules · 270 screens · 45
personas · 143 AI capabilities · 28 screen archetypes · 10 layers.**

The product's differentiator is **AI embedded in every module**, and this
document is structured so that claim is *checkable* rather than asserted: every
screen specification names at least one AI touchpoint, every touchpoint names its
affordance pattern, its human-in-the-loop gate, its confidence treatment, its
explainability surface, its guardrail and its audit event.

> **⚠️ Conventions freeze.** §0 and §1 define every vocabulary this document
> uses. They were written before any screen and **must not be changed** — ~1,900
> downstream references resolve against them. Adding a term is fine; changing or
> renumbering one is not. See §0.4.

---

## §0 How to read this document

### §0.1 Who this is for, and the reading path per role

This document has four audiences and they should not read it the same way.

| If you are… | Read | Skip |
|---|---|---|
| **A designer producing mockups** | §1 (notation) → §5 (design system) → §6 (global patterns) → §8 (sample data) → §10 (archetypes + production plan) → §9 (registry) → then your assigned module's `M-xx.4` and `M-xx.10` | §3 beyond your personas · §7 detail · all other modules |
| **The presenter running the client meeting** | §2 (client context) → §10.2 (deck storyline) → §4.1 (the AI story in one page) → M-18 (the flagship) → each module's `M-xx.5` **module AI narrative**, which is written as two sentences you can say out loud | every screen spec |
| **A product or clinical reviewer** | §2.4 (out of scope) → §7 (compliance) → each module's `M-xx.1` (purpose and boundary) and `M-xx.9` (workflows) → §G (open questions) | §5 · §10 · wireframes |
| **An engineer sizing the build** | §1.2 (namespaces) → §E (what carries over from the existing corpus) → `M-xx.3`, `M-xx.7`, `M-xx.8` for every module → §G (design decisions) | wireframes · accessibility notes · drawing notes |

**The fastest useful path** for anyone is §10.2, the 29-screen deck storyline. It
names the exact screens, in presentation order, that carry the client meeting. If
you only ever produce 29 mockups, produce those.

### §0.2 What this document is — and is not

**It is** a UI specification and mockup brief. Its unit of work is the *screen*.
It states, for every screen, what is on it, who may see it, what they can do,
what happens when they do, what it looks like when things go wrong, and where the
AI appears.

**It is not** any of the following, and reading it as one of them will mislead:

| Not a… | Because | Where that lives instead |
|---|---|---|
| Data model or schema | Entities appear only as *what the user sees* (`M-xx.8`), with display formats, not column types, nullability or keys | To be written; `§G` `DD-005` is the decision it hangs off |
| API specification | Routes here are **client-side UI routes**, not endpoints. `/ip/beds` is a screen address | `docs/INTERFACE_CONTRACTS.md` covers the existing contracts |
| Requirements document | No requirement IDs, no traceability to a source spec, no acceptance criteria. Statements here are *design intent* | `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`, for the existing patient-portal product only |
| Build plan or estimate | No sequencing, sizing, dependencies or phasing of *implementation*. The passes in `§0.5` sequence the *document* | Not yet written |
| Commitment to the client | Every number about Indostates Health in §2.1 is a **stated assumption**, flagged as such and logged in §G | §2.1, §G |

**One more absence, stated deliberately.** This document specifies no AI model,
prompt, threshold, vendor or training set. It specifies *touchpoints* — where AI
appears, what it may do, and what a human must do about it. That separation is
`DD-008`, and it is what keeps 143 AI capabilities coherent instead of 27
modules each inventing their own AI idea.

**The completeness guarantee, and how to check it.** Three sets must reconcile
exactly: the screen IDs in the §9 registry · the `#### S-mm-nn` specification
headings in Part 2 · the screen IDs referenced anywhere else. A screen in the
registry with no specification is a gap; a specification not in the registry is
an orphan. Neither is permitted. The same holds for `AI-`, `P-`, `C-`, `GP-`,

⚠️ **This is enforced, not reviewed.** Run:

```text
python3 docs/verify_ui_atlas.py
```

It asserts 36 invariants — reference resolution in both directions, every
module's `M-xx.4` inventory against §9, all 14 state codes in every screen spec,
the `AI-911` row and `Z7b` line on every screen, the deck storyline against the
T1 set, no `$` amounts, no `MM/DD` dates, no cash-handling UI, and markdown
table integrity. **Run it after any edit.** Because this document will be split
across a mockup, a web app and a mobile app, an inconsistency introduced here
becomes three inconsistencies later. §G.3 records the current result.

### §0.4 Conventions freeze — what may not change after Pass 0

Everything in §0 and §1 was written before any screen specification, because a
screen written late must use the same vocabulary as one written early. These are
frozen:

1. **ID namespaces and their formats** (§1.2) — including zero-padding.
2. **The 14 screen state codes** (§1.5) — a closed set. A screen may declare a
   state `n/a` with a stated reason; it may not invent a fifteenth.
3. **The 8 layout zones** `Z1`–`Z8` (§5.2) — a closed set.
4. **The 5 gate levels** `G0`–`G4` (§4.4) — a closed set.
5. **The 3 confidence bands** and **5 dispositions** (§4.5, §4.6) — closed sets.
6. **The 10 AI affordance patterns** (§4.3) — 10 more are reserved.
7. **Every allocated ID.** IDs are never reused and never renumbered. A
   withdrawn screen keeps its row and is marked `⊘ withdrawn` with a reason —
   the same named-absence habit the existing corpus uses, and for the same
   reason: a silent deletion is indistinguishable from an oversight.

**What may still change:** screen names, routes, tier assignments, field lists,
wireframes, and anything inside a `M-xx.10` specification. Those are content.

### §0.5 Authoring passes & change log

The document was written in seven passes. Pass 0 writes no screen content at
all — it writes the vocabularies and allocates every ID, which is why nothing
downstream ever renumbers.

| Pass | Writes | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | §0 · §1 · §2 · module index · §9 registry with every screen ID allocated | ✅ |
| **1** | §3 personas · §4 AI fabric · §5 design system · §6 global patterns · §7 compliance · §8 sample data · §10 archetypes + production plan | ✅ |
| **2** | All 28 module headers (`M-xx.1` … `M-xx.8`) — no screens, no workflows | ✅ |
| **3** | All 109 workflows (`M-xx.9`) | ✅ |
| **4** | `M-xx.10` screen specs — all 270 screens, generated from one template so the structure is identical across every module | ✅ |
| **5** | `M-28` AI Assistant & Portal Chatbots — 14 per-portal assistants · `GP-17` assistant bubble (§6.1) | ✅ |
| **6** | Appendices §A … §G — reverse indexes, reuse map, glossary, `DD` and `OQ` registers, reconciliation record | ✅ |

**Why the specs were generated rather than hand-written.** 270 screens
hand-authored independently would drift — a state missing here, an AI gate
inconsistent there, and the modules would not combine into one product. Instead
every `M-xx.10` block is produced from a single template that derives its AI
touchpoint rows from the owning module's `M-xx.5` table and its workflow
back-references from the `W-` step tables. That is why **every screen carries all
14 state codes, an `AI-911` row and a `Z7b` line**, and why `M-xx.4` can never
disagree with §9. The consistency is structural, not reviewed.

Writing all module boundaries together in Pass 2 is what surfaces ownership
overlaps ("who owns the discharge summary?") while moving a screen between
modules still costs one registry row. Writing all workflows in Pass 3, *before*
any screen specification, is what reveals missing screens — adding a registry row
in Pass 3 costs a line; discovering the same gap in Pass 7 costs a renumber,
which §0.4 forbids.

| `Zn` | `Z5` | Layout zone 🔒 | Z1 … Z8 | closed set | §5.2 |

**Three hard rules.**

1. **Zero-pad always.** `M-01`, never `M-1` — otherwise a search for `M-1`
   matches M-1, M-10 through M-19, and nothing is findable.
2. **Every ID is a unique search token.** No ID is a prefix of a different ID in
   the same namespace at the same length.
3. **No ID is ever reused or renumbered.** §0.4, rule 7.

### §1.3 Cross-reference convention

**Definitions are headings; references are bare IDs.** This document does not use
markdown anchor links for its ~1,900 internal references, because anchor slugs
differ between GitHub, VS Code, pandoc and terminal viewers and there is no way
to verify 1,900 of them. Instead:

- **Definition site** — the ID *starts a heading*: `#### S-07-04 · Inpatient Progress Note`
- **Reference site** — the bare ID in prose or a table cell: `S-07-04`

So `grep -n "^#### S-07-04"` finds the definition, and `grep -n "S-07-04"` finds
the definition plus every reference. This behaves identically in a terminal, an
editor, on GitHub and in a printed PDF. Anchor links are used **only** for the
~40 `##`-level headings, from the table of contents.

### §1.4 Data flow notation

Carried over unchanged from `docs/DOMAIN_MAP.md`, so the two documents' flow
tables can be read together.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **→** | Outbound: this module writes to, or calls, the counterpart |
| **←** | Inbound: this module reads from, or is called by, the counterpart |
| **↔** | Bidirectional |
| **⊘** | Flow specified but currently blocked or out of phase |

In workflow step tables, `→` additionally means "navigates to", and `←` "returns
to". Actor micro-syntax in a `What happens` cell: **`U:`** the user acts ·
**`S:`** this system acts · **`X:`** an external system acts.

### §1.5 Screen state codes 🔒

A closed set of 14. Every screen specification carries a state table with a row
for each. A screen may state a code `n/a` — but only **with a reason**, because
an unexplained omission is indistinguishable from an oversight.

| Code | Trigger | What it means for the mockup |
|---|---|---|
| `LOADING` | first paint, data in flight | skeleton geometry that matches the loaded layout — never a spinner on a blank page |
| `EMPTY` | no data, legitimately | explain *why* it is empty and what to do; never a bare "No records" |
| `PARTIAL` | some regions loaded, one failed | the screen stays usable; the failed region says what is missing and since when |
| `ERROR` | the operation failed | recoverable, with the user's input preserved and an escape hatch |
| `VALIDATION` | user submitted with gaps | count of problems, inline errors, focus moved to the first, primary action stays disabled |
| `DENIED` | caller lacks the capability | what is missing, who grants it, a request action — **and no patient data anywhere on screen** |
| `BREAKGLASS` | has capability, lacks relationship | amber full-width banner, reason required before content renders, "this access is logged and reviewed" |
| `OFFLINE` | network unavailable | what still works, what is queued, what is blocked. Typed content is never lost |
| `STALE` | cached data past its freshness budget | timestamp turns amber, "Data as of HH:MM · Refresh" |
| `SAVING` | write in flight | primary action disabled, content **not** locked |
| `LOCKED` | record signed, or held by another user | read-only render naming who and when, plus the legitimate next action (addendum, refresh) |
| `AI-OFF` | AI service down, or disabled for this tenant | every `◆` affordance **hidden entirely, not greyed**; one quiet line; the screen fully usable |
| `AI-ABSTAIN` | AI cannot produce a calibrated answer | states what is missing; **never** a null score, a zero, or a blank band |
| `AI-LOW` | confidence band is LOW | delivered collapsed with an amber band; acceptance blocked until expanded |

The last three exist because "AI in every module" creates a failure surface in
every module. A product that degrades gracefully when its AI is unavailable is a
different product from one that does not, and the difference is visible only if
the states are drawn.

### §1.6 Field-type dictionary

The vocabulary a field table's `Type` column may use. Fixed, so a designer never
has to guess what control to draw.

| Type | Control | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | single-line input | |
| `textarea` | multi-line, autogrow | row count stated per field |
| `rich` | formatted text with a minimal toolbar | clinical notes only |
| `number` | numeric input with unit suffix | unit always shown, never implied |
| `select` | dropdown, single | ≤12 options; source list named |
| `multiselect` | dropdown, multiple, chips below | |
| `combobox` | typeahead with a constrained list | >12 options, or a coded set |
| `typeahead` | free search against a coded terminology | SNOMED/ICD/LOINC/drug master |
| `radio` | radio group | ≤5 mutually exclusive options |
| `checkbox` | single boolean | |
| `checkgroup` | multiple booleans | |
| `date` · `time` · `datetime` | pickers | format per §5.4; **never** `MM/DD` |
| `duration` | value + unit pair | |
| `money` | ₹ input, lakh grouping | §5.4 |
| `phone` | +91-prefixed, 10-digit validated | |
| `abha` | 14-digit ABHA number or `name@abdm` address | §7.1 |
| `file` | upload with type and size constraints | malware-scan gate per `CMP-DPDP-06` |
| `signature` | draw / Aadhaar eSign / DSC / thumb impression | §5.8, `CMP-NABH-11` |
| `barcode` | scan-first with keyed fallback | fallback is never removed |
| `readonly` | displayed value, not editable | source and timestamp always shown |
| `computed` | derived, not editable | the derivation is stated |
| `tiles` | a read-only value grid | vitals, results |
| `slider` | bounded scale | pain scores, triage scales |
| `toggle` | immediate-effect boolean | no save button |

Requirement markers in a field table's `Req` column: ✅ mandatory · 🟡
conditionally mandatory (the condition is stated) · — optional.

### §1.7 Priority tiers

The tier decides how much specification a screen gets, and what the mockup
deliverable is. It is the lever that makes 256 screens fit one document.

| Tier | Count | Specification | Mockup deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | 29 | FULL template, hand-polished, wireframe mandatory | High-fidelity, both themes, the states named in §10.4 |
| **T2** | 138 | FULL template | High-fidelity, light theme, default + one notable state |
| **T3** | 103 | BRIEF template | Mid-fidelity or a component composition; drawn only if the deck needs it |

T1 is exactly the 29 screens of the deck storyline in §10.2. A screen's tier is
about *presentation priority*, not build priority — a T3 screen may still be
essential to ship.

### §1.9 Formatting rules for authors

These keep the file greppable and renderable at 15,000 lines.

- Prose wraps at **80 columns**, matching the existing corpus.
- Table rows may exceed 80 columns, but **no single cell exceeds ~90
  characters**. Longer content becomes a bold-label paragraph below the table.
- Escape pipes inside cells as `\|` — the existing corpus's habit.
- **No nested tables.** No HTML except the `<!-- /M-xx -->` module fences.
- Fenced code blocks are reserved for **wireframes**, use ` ```text `, are
  **ASCII-only** and **≤100 columns**.
- Inside a wireframe, write `<>` where the product shows `◆` — the diamond is
  double-width in some terminals and destroys column alignment.
- **No heading deeper than `####`.** Inside a screen or workflow, sub-blocks are
  **bold labels**, not headings. This is what keeps a generated table of
  contents usable at 256 screens.
- `---` before every `##`.
- `·` (middot) separates items in an inline list; `§` prefixes a section
  reference.

| A3 | **PM-JAY empanelled**, with TPA cashless, CGHS and ESI all in the payer mix; roughly 40% scheme, 35% cashless, 25% cash | M-19, M-20 screen weight and the order of the revenue-cycle story | `OQ-503` |
| A4 | **NABH-aspiring**, not yet accredited | Whether M-24 is a Phase-1 differentiator or Phase-3 hygiene | `OQ-504` |
| A5 | **ABDM HIP-registered**, ABHA linkage live but low adoption | The prominence of Scan & Share (`S-04-02`) and the publish-failure queue | `OQ-505` |
| A6 | Launch languages **English + Hindi + one regional**; patient-facing documents bilingual | §5.4 typography, `GP-08`, every patient-facing screen | `OQ-506` |
| A7 | **India-only data residency**, which constrains every model and vendor choice | `DD-009`, M-25 AI governance | `OQ-507` |

| A9 | Unreliable power and connectivity at secondary sites is **normal, not exceptional** | `DD-015`, the `OFFLINE` state on every screen, downtime forms | `OQ-509` |

**Confirmed client policies** — unlike the table above, these are **stated by
the client**, not assumed. They are listed separately so nobody treats them as

| # | Policy | Consequence for the design |
|---|---|---|
| **A10** | ⚠️ **Digital payment modes only — no cash is accepted.** UPI, QR, card, POS and netbanking, plus payer and scheme settlement | No cash tender, cash drawer, petty-cash float or denomination-wise shift close anywhere in the product. `S-19-01` is a **collection** counter, not a cash counter; `S-19-10` reconciles **gateway settlement**, not notes. Self-funding patients are labelled **"self-pay"**, never "cash". §8.4's payer mix and every billing mockup follow this |

### §2.2 What the client must feel after the presentation

The designer is producing a **sales artefact**, not only a build specification,
and needs to know what it has to accomplish. Four things, in order:

1. **"They understand a hospital."** The screens show attendant passes, UPI
   and POS collection, MLC registers, ward-class tariff differentials, Form F,
   discharge waiting on TPA approval, and a downtime form. Nothing reads as a US product
   with rupees pasted over the dollars. This is what earns the second meeting.
2. **"The AI is everywhere, and it is governed."** A `◆` on a value in nearly
   every screenshot, and — just as important — visible accept/reject controls,
   confidence bands, a `Why?` link, and one screen where **the AI is overruled by
   a hard rule**. An ungoverned AI demo frightens a medical superintendent; a
   governed one reassures them.
3. **"The stroke centre is real."** M-18 is not a dashboard with a map. It is a
   clock, a parallel task board, a spoke console designed for a general physician
   at 02:00, and a 90-day outcome follow-up campaign. Specificity is the proof.
4. **"They have thought about what breaks."** The offline strip, the break-glass
   banner, the AI-abstain state, the publish-failure queue. Every buyer has been
   burned by a demo that only worked on the happy path.

**What must *not* happen:** 29 mockups showing 29 different patients with
inconsistent names, ID formats and currency. That is the single most common way a
deck stops reading as one product — and it is why §8 exists and is mandatory.

### §2.3 The differentiator, stated once

Most hospital systems that claim AI have bolted a handful of models onto a
records product: a chatbot, a no-show predictor, a coding assistant. The claim
here is structural rather than additive, and rests on three properties:

**One fabric, not 27 integrations.** Every AI capability lives in a single
catalogue (§4.2) organised into nine families. No module owns a model, a prompt,
a threshold or a training set — modules own **touchpoints** that compose from the
fabric. This is `DD-008`, and it is the same discipline the existing corpus
applies to external vendors through its adapter modules.

**One interaction language.** Ten affordance patterns, five gate levels, three
confidence bands, five dispositions, one explainability drawer with four fixed
panels, one `◆` glyph. A clinician who learns how to accept an AI suggestion in
the outpatient note already knows how to accept one in the bed board, the coding
queue and the stroke console. Consistency is a clinical-safety property, not a
cosmetic one.

**One governance surface.** Every AI action emits an audit event with a fixed
payload (§4.9). Model health, drift, override rates and per-site performance are
visible on a screen someone is accountable for (`S-25-06`, `S-25-07`). And the
top autonomy tier — autonomous **and** irreversible — is **named and forbidden
product-wide**, which is precisely what makes the five permitted tiers credible
to a clinical governance committee.

The presenter's one-line version: *"Every module has AI in it, every AI output
has a human gate on it, and you can see on one screen whether any of it is
working."*

### §2.4 Explicitly out of scope

Naming absences is more useful than implying completeness.

| Out of scope | Why |
|---|---|
| Research & clinical-trial management, CTRI, ethics-committee workflow | A separate product surface; listed as a Phase-3 candidate only |
| Academic / medical-college administration, student records | Different buyer, different regulator |
| Hospital construction, project management, CAPEX planning | Outside the clinical and operational envelope |
| Marketing automation, CRM campaign management, lead scoring | Referenced from M-26 but not specified |
| Payroll *disbursement* and core banking integration | M-23 computes and produces the instruction; the bank rail is an adapter |
| Full ERP general ledger, statutory financial accounting | M-19 posts outbound to a GL; the GL itself is external |
| Native in-app video *rendering* and any vendor SDK internals | M-27 orchestrates sessions through an adapter, consistent with the existing corpus |
| Device firmware, modality calibration software | M-21 tracks assets and calibration *records*, not the instruments |
| Any AI model, prompt, threshold, vendor or training set | §0.2, `DD-008` |
| Data model, API contracts, schema, migrations | §0.2 |

### §2.6 Layer dependency rule

A module may depend on its own layer and any layer above it in this list. A
dependency that runs the other way is an error, and the four that exist are
declared exceptions, named in the module that owns them.

```text
   A  Platform          M-01 M-02 M-03      depends on nothing
   B  Access to care    M-04 M-05           depends on A
   C  Clinical core     M-06 ... M-13       depends on A B
   D  Diagnostics       M-14 ... M-17       depends on A B C
   E  Flagship          M-18                depends on A B C D
   F  Revenue cycle     M-19 M-20           depends on A B C D
   G  Operations        M-21 M-22 M-23      depends on A
   H  Governance        M-24 M-25           depends on all
   I  Patient channels  M-26 M-27           depends on A B C F
   J  Assistance       M-28                depends on all
```

**Declared exceptions** — four upward dependencies that are real and deliberate:

| Exception | Direction | Why it is permitted |
|---|---|---|
| `M-02` reads privileging status from `M-23` | A ← G | Clinical privileging is an HR fact with an authorization consequence. `M-02` reads it; it never writes it. Carries `DEC-004`'s F-16 |
| `M-03` publishes to ABDM on `M-13` events | A ← C | The publish *trigger* is clinical; the publish *mechanism* is platform. `M-03` subscribes, it does not reach into `M-13` |
| `M-01` bed inventory is read by `M-08` | A → C | Normal direction; noted because bed *inventory* (config) and bed *state* (clinical) are easily confused. `M-01` owns the bed exists; `M-08` owns who is in it |
| `M-18` reads live resource state from `M-08`, `M-11`, `M-22` | E ← C, G | Single-act reservation (`S-18-14`) must hold a bed, a cath lab and an ambulance atomically. This is the exception that justifies itself — see `DD-012` |

## §3 Personas & permissions

### §3.1 Persona catalogue

45 personas. A persona is **not** a role and not a permission — it is a person
with a job, a device and an environment. Authorization is capability-based and
subject-scoped (§3.2), so a persona here maps to a *set* of capability grants,
never to a single role name.

**The identity rule that makes 45 personas affordable:** one person is one
`Party`, and every role they hold is a separate time-bounded record. A
consultant who is also a department head and a member of the pharmacy committee
holds three role records, not one composite role. This carries `DEC-001`
constraint D-4 from the existing corpus unchanged — see §E.

**Four personas drive design decisions the others do not**, and they are worth
naming because forgetting them is how hospital software fails in India:

- **`P-35` the on-call stroke neurologist** is the only persona whose *primary*
  device is a phone at 02:00. `S-18-14` and `S-18-11` are designed phone-first
  and wall-second — the inverse of every other screen in the product.
- **`P-38` the spoke-site physician** is usually *not* a neurologist and is
  usually *alone*. `S-18-13` deliberately asks for six fields, not sixty. A
  console designed for a hub specialist would go unused at the spoke, and an
  unused spoke console means the network does not exist.
- **`P-29` the housekeeping supervisor** may have limited literacy in English.
  Their screens are icon-and-colour first, with text as reinforcement — which is
  a different design, not a simplified one.
- **`P-45` the external auditor** gets read-only, time-boxed, fully-logged
  access. `S-24-02` exists so that a NABH surveillance question is answered in
  four clicks rather than four days of file-pulling. That capability is worth
  money to the client and is invisible unless someone drew it.

**Reserved and unused:** `P-46` … `P-60`. Likely additions: chaplain / medical
social worker, interpreter, medical tourism coordinator, research coordinator,
vendor technician with escorted access.

### §3.2 Permission model & verb matrix

**Three rules, carried unchanged from the existing corpus's `DEC-003`** and
restated here because every `Permission` line in a screen spec depends on them:

1. **No authorization check compares a role name.** Enforcement reads
   **capabilities**. `P-04 Consultant` is a persona label for humans reading this
   document; the system checks `ip.note.write`, never `role == consultant`.
2. **Every decision is evaluated within a subject scope.** "May Dr Iyer read a
   chart" is not a question. "May Dr Iyer read *this patient's* chart" is. The
   subject is a patient, an encounter, a facility or a unit.
3. **Default is deny**, and authority is evaluated **at request time** — never
   baked into a token at sign-in.

Capability names follow `<domain>.<object>.<verb>`. The verbs are a closed set:

| Verb | Means | Notable |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | View | The most-granted, most-audited verb |
| `write` | Create or update a draft | Does not imply `sign` |
| `sign` | Attest and commit to the legal record | Requires identity + timestamp; irreversible |
| `cosign` | Counter-attest another's entry | Held by a narrower set than `sign` |
| `amend` | Add an addendum to a signed record | **Never** an in-place edit — `CMP-NABH-10` |
| `cancel` | Void a not-yet-actioned item | Reason mandatory |
| `approve` | Release a queued item to the next stage | Pre-auth, leave, purchase, result release |
| `override` | Proceed past a soft block | Reason mandatory, always audited |
| `admin` | Configure the module | Never implies clinical `read` |
| `export` | Extract beyond the screen | Always a class-3 audit event |

**The four scope qualifiers** a capability is evaluated against:

| Scope | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `self` | The authenticated subject's own data | `P-33` reading their own record |
| `relationship` | A care relationship exists between actor and patient | `P-04` on their own inpatient |
| `unit` | Actor is rostered to the ward, theatre or department | `P-07` on their ward's beds |
| `facility` | Actor holds the capability across one facility | `P-09` on the bed board |
| `group` | Across all facilities | `P-01` on roll-ups only; never clinical detail |

**⚠️ Two hazards a designer must draw, not assume:**

**Break-glass** (`BREAKGLASS` state, `GP-11`, `S-02-05`). An actor with the
capability but **no relationship** is not refused — they are offered
break-glass: state a reason, proceed, and the access is logged and reviewed
within 24 hours. This exists because the alternative is a system that can block
a code stroke, and *an authorization model that can block resuscitation is the
wrong model*. See `DD-014`.

**Uniform refusal.** When access is refused, the message is **identical across
every cause in its class** — no relationship, no such patient, patient in
another facility, record sealed. A refusal that distinguishes causes is a
relationship-existence oracle: "no such patient" versus "not your patient" leaks
that the patient exists. This carries `DEC-005` and `DEC-009` K-1/K-2. The
`DENIED` state therefore shows **no patient data at all**, which is why §1.5
states that explicitly.

### §3.3 Device, density & environment

Three density modes, selected per persona (§3.1) and overridable by the user.
Density is not a cosmetic preference — `P-13` reading 80 studies in a session and
`P-01` reading six tiles need genuinely different information density.

| Mode | Row height | Base type | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compact | 32px | 13px | Worklists, boards, flowsheets, counters |
| Comfortable | 40px | 14px | Dashboards, forms, patient-facing |
| Wall | 56px+ | 18px+ | `ARC-12` command walls — readable at 4 metres |

**Environment constraints that change the design**, not just the styling:

| Environment | Personas | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Gloved hands | P-07, P-10, P-16, P-17 | Touch targets ≥44px; no hover-only affordance; no drag-and-drop as the only path |
| Dark reading room | P-13 | Night theme is the **default**, not an option; no large white fields |
| Moving vehicle | P-39 | One-handed, ≤60s to complete, works at 2G, survives signal loss mid-form |
| Standing queue behind | P-03, P-21 | Keyboard-first, no mouse round-trips, every screen has a ≤4-keystroke happy path |
| 02:00 at home on a phone | P-35 | Phone-first layout, push-notification entry, no dependence on a second monitor |
| Poor bandwidth | P-38, P-39 | Images degrade progressively; the clinical decision never waits on a full-resolution series |
| Low literacy in English | P-29, some P-33 | Icon + colour + regional-language text; never text alone |
| Time-boxed inspection | P-45 | Evidence reachable in ≤4 clicks from a standard reference |

## §4 The AI fabric

### §4.1 The AI story in one page

**The claim.** AI is in all 28 modules — 143 capabilities, at least one on every
one of the 270 screens, and `AI-911` on **all** of them. **The reason it is not 27 bolted-on features** is that
the AI lives in one fabric with one interaction language and one governance
surface, and modules compose from it rather than owning any of it.

**`DD-008`, the structural rule:** *no module owns a model, a prompt, a
threshold or a training set.* Modules own **touchpoints**. A touchpoint is a
place on a screen where a fabric capability surfaces, and it is fully described
by seven answers — which is the checklist that keeps 142 capabilities coherent
instead of 142 opinions:

| # | Question | Vocabulary | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which capability? | `AI-fnn` | §4.2 |
| 2 | How does it look? | `AIP-01` … `AIP-10` | §4.3 |
| 3 | What must the human do? | `G0` … `G4` | §4.4 |
| 4 | How is uncertainty shown? | HIGH / MED / LOW | §4.5 |
| 5 | What can the human do about it? | 5 dispositions | §4.6 |
| 6 | How is it explained? | `C-42`, four fixed panels | §4.7 |
| 7 | What stops it going wrong, and what is recorded? | guardrail + audit event | §4.8, §4.9 |

**Four standing guardrails**, stated once and binding on all 142 capabilities:

1. **AI is never the only path to completing a clinical task.** Every AI feature
   declares a fallback, and §1.5's `AI-OFF` state must be drawn on every screen.
   A model outage degrades the product; it never stops care.
2. **Hard rules are enforced deterministically.** Allergy stops, isolation
   requirements, PM-JAY bed-class entitlement, PCPNDT Form F, controlled-drug
   limits. **AI may rank *within* these constraints; it may never rank
   *around* them.** This is the single most important sentence in §4 for a
   clinical governance committee, and `S-06-07` and `S-08-05` are the screens
   that demonstrate it.
3. **Nothing AI-generated enters the legal medical record unsigned.** Every
   `G2`-and-above output requires a recorded disposition before it persists.
4. **Autonomy tier T5 — autonomous *and* irreversible — is forbidden
   product-wide.** Naming the tier and prohibiting it is precisely what makes the
   five permitted tiers credible. See §4.4.

**The presenter's line:** *"Every module has AI in it, every AI output has a
human gate on it, and one screen tells you whether any of it is still working."*
That screen is `S-25-07`.

### §4.2 AI capability catalogue

143 capabilities in nine family blocks. The block is load-bearing: a reader
seeing `◆AI-512` knows immediately it is revenue-cycle AI, and
`grep '◆AI-2'` returns every clinical-decision-support touchpoint in the
document. Sequential numbering would lose that; blocks cost nothing.

Every capability below is referenced by at least one screen in §9, and every AI
ID referenced in §9 appears below — verified mechanically, see §9.10. `AI-911`
is the one capability present on **every** screen, because `GP-17` is a global
pattern rather than a per-screen feature.

**Columns.** `Gate` is the *maximum* gate at which the capability may be used;
an individual touchpoint may be stricter but never looser. `Fallback` is what
the screen does when the capability is unavailable — required by guardrail 1.

whose failure has a **patient-safety** consequence rather than an efficiency one;
their `Fallback` column says "never fully off" because a deterministic
rule-based floor remains even when the model is unavailable. Second,
`AI-909`'s fallback is deliberately `⊘ none` — a monitoring capability cannot
monitor itself, so its unavailability triggers the global kill switch (§4.8)
rather than a degraded mode. Naming that rather than inventing a fallback is the
honest answer.

capability from each family. The spread is the evidence that the fabric is not a
handful of models in three modules:

### §4.3 AI affordance patterns 🔒

Ten patterns. This is *how AI looks*, held separately from *what AI does*
(§4.2) and *what the human must do* (§4.4) — three small closed vocabularies
that compose to describe any touchpoint in one table row.

| ID | Pattern | Use when | Drawn as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AIP-01` | Inline ghost content | AI drafts text the user will own | 85% opacity, left accent rule in AI-indigo, `C-41` action bar beneath. **Ghost text sits *in* the field, not in a side card** |
| `AIP-02` | Inline field chip | AI fills one structured value | Chip inside the field: `◆` + confidence dot + ✓/✕ |
| `AIP-03` | Suggestion card | Discrete, rankable proposals | `Z6` card, evidence line, per-card accept / edit / dismiss |
| `AIP-04` | Side panel | Conversational or exploratory AI | `Z6` 320px panel, `C-40` |
| `AIP-05` | Banner / strip | Something the user must notice now | `Z3` or `Z4` full-width strip, severity-coloured, `Why?` link |
| `AIP-06` | List / row badge | Per-record score in a collection | Badge + band dot, sortable, tooltip on hover and focus |
| `AIP-07` | Ranked or reordered list | AI changes order, not content | `Sorted by AI acuity ▾` header control + per-row reason chip. **Always reversible to a deterministic sort** |
| `AIP-08` | Explainability drawer | Invoked from any of the above | `C-42`, right drawer 480px, four fixed panels (§4.7) |
| `AIP-09` | Modal gate | AI output must be resolved before proceeding | `C-31` modal, not dismissible without a disposition |
| `AIP-10` | Ambient / invisible | AI improves a result with no surface | No visual. Disclosed only in §4.2 and on `S-25-08` |

**`AIP-07`'s reversibility rule is not optional.** A clinician who cannot get
back to a predictable ordering will stop trusting the list, and a worklist
nobody trusts is worse than an unsorted one. Every AI-sorted list ships with a
visible, one-click deterministic sort.

**`AIP-10` needs the disclosure to be real.** An AI touchpoint with no visual
surface is the easiest place to lose a patient's trust, so every `AIP-10` use is
enumerated on `S-25-08` — the transparency register — and nowhere else in the
product is it permitted to be silent.

### §4.4 The human-in-the-loop gate ladder 🔒

Exactly **one** gate per touchpoint. The gate determines the UI treatment
completely, so a designer never has to decide how much friction an AI feature
deserves — §4.2 already said.

| Gate | Name | The human must… | Fixed UI treatment | Permitted for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`G0`** | Ambient | Nothing | Disclosure only — a `Sorted by AI` label or an §4.2 entry. **Never a dialog** | Non-clinical ranking, search, cosmetics |
| **`G1`** | Suggest | Notice; may ignore | `AIP-05` / `AIP-06`; dismissible; optional "not useful" + reason | Risk scores, nudges, forecasts |
| **`G2`** | Confirm | Accept / Edit / Reject **before the value is committed** | `C-41` action bar. **The page's primary action stays disabled until every `G2` item has a disposition** | Drafts, codes, order suggestions, allocations |
| **`G3`** | Attest | Accept **and** sign, with identity and timestamp recorded | `C-41` + signature block + a fixed-wording "I have reviewed this content" checkbox | Anything entering the legal medical record or a claim |
| **`G4`** | Dual | A second qualified user must co-sign | `C-31` modal + second-user authentication; reason mandatory; **both** identities recorded | Overrides of hard stops, high-risk dosing, AI-initiated escalation |
| **`T5`** | — | ⊘ **Forbidden product-wide** | — | Autonomous **and** irreversible action. Named here so that its prohibition is explicit and auditable |

**The one-sentence rule that removes ambiguity from 183 screens:** *no `G2`-or-
above AI output is persisted without a recorded disposition.* It is stated here
and never repeated in a screen spec.

**Why `T5` is in the table.** A governance committee's first question is "what
can this thing do without us?" An architecture that cannot answer "nothing
irreversible, ever, by construction" will be approved slowly or not at all.
Listing the tier and forbidding it is cheaper than arguing the point 27 times.

### §4.5 Confidence bands 🔒

Three bands. **Never a bare number.**

| Band | Range | Rendered as | Delivery behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HIGH** | ≥ 0.85 | Solid indigo dot + "High confidence" | May be delivered pre-expanded |
| **MED** | 0.60 – 0.84 | Half amber dot + "Moderate confidence" | Delivered expanded, **no pre-selection** |
| **LOW** | < 0.60 | Hollow amber ring + "Low confidence — review closely" | Delivered **collapsed**; acceptance blocked until expanded |

Three rules: a percentage may *accompany* the band label but never replace it ·
`G0` touchpoints show no confidence at all · and a capability that cannot produce
a calibrated score shows **`AI-ABSTAIN`**, not LOW.

**The abstain rule matters more than it looks.** A risk score of 0 because there
are no vitals and a risk score of 0 because the patient is well are clinically
opposite and visually identical. `AI-ABSTAIN` states *what is missing* —
"Cannot assess: no vitals since 02:10" — and offers the action that would fix it.

### §4.6 Disposition vocabulary 🔒

A closed set of five. Each has exactly one control in `C-41` and exactly one
audit record. **No module invents a sixth.**

| Disposition | Means | Reason required? |
|---|---|---|
| `Accepted` | Taken as offered | No |
| `Accepted with edits` | Taken and modified; the diff is retained | No |
| `Rejected` | Discarded | **Yes** — fixed 5-value list + Other |
| `Deferred` | Left undecided; the item persists in a queue | No |
| `Overridden` | `G4` only — proceeded past a hard stop | **Yes**, + co-signer identity |

The five rejection reasons, fixed so the feedback is analysable on `S-25-07`:
*clinically incorrect · not relevant to this patient · already documented ·
insufficient information · other (free text)*.

### §4.7 Explainability — `C-42`, four fixed panels

Identical on every screen, so a clinician learns it once. **Mandatory for
`G1`–`G4`; on-demand only for `G0`.**

| Panel | Contains | Why it is non-negotiable |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · What this is** | Plain-language claim, confidence band, timestamp | The claim must be legible without the model |
| **2 · What it used** | The inputs, each clickable back to its source record | **This is the panel that earns clinical trust.** A clinician who can see the score used a 4-hour-old BP will calibrate correctly |
| **3 · Why** | Top drivers with direction and weight, or the retrieved evidence / pathway citation. **Never raw feature names** | "Rising respiratory rate" is usable; `feat_rr_delta_4h` is not |
| **4 · Limits & provenance** | Model name, version, validation population, known failure modes, a "not a diagnosis" line, and a `Report a problem` action | Per-site validation matters — a model validated at the hub may not hold at a tier-3 spoke |

### §4.8 Guardrails, abstention & the three failure states

Every capability in §4.2 carries a one-line guardrail. Beyond those, four
system-level controls:

| Control | Owner | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Per-capability kill switch** | `S-25-06` | Disables one `AI-fnn` across the group or one facility. Screens fall to `AI-OFF` |
| **Global kill switch** | `S-25-06` | Disables the entire fabric. Every screen remains fully usable |
| **Per-site enablement** | `S-25-06` | A capability may be live at the hub and off at a spoke, because validation is per-site |
| **Auto-abstain thresholds** | `S-25-06` | Input-completeness floors below which a capability declines to answer |

**The three failure states, drawn on every screen** (§1.5):

- **`AI-OFF`** — affordances **hidden entirely, never greyed**. A greyed control
  advertises a missing feature and invites a support call; a hidden one leaves a
  working screen. One quiet line: "AI assistance unavailable."
- **`AI-ABSTAIN`** — states what is missing and offers the fixing action.
- **`AI-LOW`** — collapsed, amber, acceptance gated on expansion.

### §4.9 AI audit taxonomy

**`DD-007` adds an eighth auditable event class** to the seven the existing
corpus defines in `DEC-008`: **AI inference and AI acceptance.** Without it,
"AI everywhere" is unauditable and therefore indefensible to a regulator or a
plaintiff.

Event names are fixed: `AI.<FAMILY3>.<VERB>`.

| Event | Emitted when |
|---|---|
| `AI.DOC.DRAFT_DISPOSITION` | A drafted note section is accepted, edited or rejected |
| `AI.CDS.RISK_ACKNOWLEDGED` | A risk or deterioration alert is acknowledged, escalated or dismissed |
| `AI.ORD.SUGGESTION_DISPOSITION` | An order or pathway suggestion is dispositioned |
| `AI.IMG.FINDING_DISPOSITION` | An imaging AI finding is confirmed or contradicted |
| `AI.RCM.CODE_DISPOSITION` | A code, package or tariff suggestion is dispositioned |
| `AI.OPS.RANKING_OVERRIDDEN` | A user reverts or re-ranks an AI-ordered list |
| `AI.SAF.HARD_STOP_OVERRIDDEN` | ⚠️ A `G4` override of a deterministic hard rule |
| `AI.GOV.CAPABILITY_TOGGLED` | A kill switch or per-site enablement changes |
| `AI.GOV.INFERENCE_SERVED` | Any inference is served — the volume denominator for §4.2's metrics |

**One fixed payload shape**, stated here and referenced by name from every
screen so that nothing is restated 183 times:

```text
actor · role-record · patient/encounter · facility · screen · AI-id ·
model@version · confidence-band · inputs-digest · disposition · reason ·
timestamp · retention-class
```

Two properties worth stating explicitly. **`inputs-digest`, not the inputs** —
the audit record must let a reviewer establish *which* data the model saw without
duplicating PHI into a second store with a different retention rule. And
**`AI.SAF.HARD_STOP_OVERRIDDEN` is the one event that must alert, not merely
record**: it is reviewed within 24 hours, on `S-25-07`.

### §4.10 AI governance surfaces

Who is accountable for the AI still working, and on which screen.

| Question | Screen | Persona |
|---|---|---|
| Which capabilities are live, where, at what version? | `S-25-06` | `P-42`, `P-25` |
| Is any model drifting, and is it worse at one site? | `S-25-07` | `P-25`, `P-02` |
| What are clinicians overriding, and why? | `S-25-07` | `P-25` |
| Is imaging AI performing per site? | `S-15-09` | `P-13`, `P-25` |
| What do we disclose to patients? | `S-25-08` | `P-43` |
| Who accessed what under break-glass? | `S-02-06` | `P-43`, `P-25` |

**Per-site reporting is the non-obvious requirement.** A model validated on hub
data may degrade at a spoke with a different scanner, a different case mix and a
different population — and in a hub-and-spoke stroke network, that is precisely
the failure that must not go unnoticed. Every metric on `S-25-07` is
breakdownable by facility, and a per-site regression is an alert rather than a
row in a monthly report.

## §5 Design system foundations

### §5.1 Layout grid, breakpoints & density

12-column fluid grid, 8px spacing base, 16px minimum side gutter on every
breakpoint.

| Breakpoint | Width | Primary personas | Layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xs` | < 768 | P-33, P-34, P-39, P-35 (on-call) | Single column. `Z2` becomes a bottom tab bar, `Z6` a bottom sheet |
| `sm` | 768 – 1023 | P-04, P-19, P-26 on tablet | Single column with an accordion; `Z2` icon rail |
| `md` | 1024 – 1279 | **P-07 ward tablet — the real bedside device** | `Z2` icon rail, `Z6` bottom sheet, `Z7` sticky |
| `lg` | 1280 – 1439 | Most desktop personas | `Z6` collapses to a 48px tab with a badge count |
| `xl` | 1440 – 1919 | P-03, P-11, P-13, P-21 | Full layout as drawn in wireframes |
| `wall` | ≥ 1920, viewed at 3–4 m | `ARC-12` only | Wall density, no `Z2`, no input affordances |

**`md` is the breakpoint that matters most and is usually designed last.** A
workstation-on-wheels at the bedside is a 1024–1280px tablet held by someone
wearing gloves. If a screen only works at `xl`, it does not work where care
happens.

### §5.2 Navigation shell & the zone vocabulary 🔒

Eight zones, a closed set. **A screen specification describes only the zones it
changes** — `Z1 Z2 Z3 — no deviation` is a legal and very common line, and it is
how 256 screens stay readable.

| Zone | Name | Default source | Height / width |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Z1` | App bar | `GP-01` — identical everywhere | 56px |
| `Z2` | Nav rail / sidebar | `GP-02` — identical everywhere | 240px, 64px collapsed |
| `Z3` | Patient context banner | `GP-05` — on **every** patient-scoped screen | 64px, 2 lines; +48px with a risk strip |
| `Z4` | Page header — breadcrumb, title, status chips, primary actions | Per screen | 64px |
| `Z5` | Main content — `Z5a`, `Z5b`… for stacked or split regions | Per screen | Fills |
| `Z6` | Right rail — AI panel, context, timeline | Per screen | 320px, collapsible |
| `Z7` | Sticky action bar / footer — `Z7a` actions, **`Z7b` assistant bubble** | Per screen; `Z7b` is global (`GP-17`) | 64px; `Z7b` is a 56px floating bubble, not a bar |
| `Z8` | Overlays — modal, drawer, toast, confirm | Per screen | Varies |

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Z1  APP BAR    facility v | search | bell | lang v | user                   |
+--------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Z2     | Z3  PATIENT CONTEXT BANNER  (patient-scoped screens only)          |
| NAV    +--------------------------------------------------------------------+
| RAIL   | Z4  PAGE HEADER   breadcrumb / title / chips / primary actions     |
|        +---------------------------------------------+----------------------+
|        | Z5  MAIN CONTENT                            | Z6  RIGHT RAIL       |
|        |     Z5a / Z5b / Z5c as needed               |     AI panel         |
|        |                                             |     context          |
|        +---------------------------------------------+----------------------+
|        | Z7a STICKY ACTION BAR                                    (Z7b) |
+--------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
   Z7b = a 56px floating assistant bubble, bottom-right, above Z7a
   Z8 overlays render above all zones (incl. the expanded GP-17 chat panel)
```

**`Z3` is the highest-leverage component in the product.** It appears on ~150
screens, it is where a wrong-patient error is caught, and it is where the
deterioration risk strip lives. It is specified once in `GP-05` and must not be
redesigned inside a screen spec.

### §5.3 Colour

**Brand.** Indostates blue `#1B4D8F` primary, `#0F2F57` dark. Used for
navigation, primary actions and identity — **never** for clinical status.

**The separation rule.** Brand colour, clinical semantics and AI are three
independent palettes that never borrow from each other. A blue that means "brand"
in `Z1` and "normal result" in `Z5` is an error waiting to happen.

| Clinical semantic | Colour | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Normal / within range | `#137547` green | Results, vitals, compliant states |
| Caution / borderline | `#B45309` amber | Near-threshold, due soon, MED confidence |
| Abnormal / high | `#B42318` red | Out of range, overdue, breach |
| ⚠️ Critical / life-threatening | `#7A0C16` deep red + icon | Critical values, hard stops, code activations |
| Isolation / infection | `#7C3AED` violet | Isolation status, HAI flags |
| Inactive / cancelled | `#667085` grey | Voided, discharged, historical |

**AI palette — deliberately outside the clinical range.** AI-indigo `#4F46E5`
for the `◆` glyph, ghost-text accent rules and suggestion cards. An AI
suggestion must never be mistakable for a clinical status, which is why indigo
appears nowhere in the semantic table above.

**⚠️ Colour is never the only carrier.** Roughly 8% of male clinicians have a
colour-vision deficiency. Every semantic state carries an **icon and a text
label** in addition to colour. An abnormal result reads `↑ High`, not a red
cell.

**Night theme** is mandatory on `S-13-*`, all `S-12-*`, all `S-18-*`, `S-15-04`
and `S-15-05`, and every `ARC-06` flowsheet — ICU, radiology reading rooms and
stroke calls happen at 03:00. Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in **both** themes.

### §5.4 Typography

| Use | Family | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Latin UI | Inter | 13px compact / 14px comfortable / 18px+ wall |
| Devanagari, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Marathi | Noto Sans (per script) | **Line height +15%** over Latin — Indic scripts have taller ascenders and descenders |
| Numerals & clinical values | Inter **tabular** figures | Non-negotiable in flowsheets and any column of numbers |
| Clocks & timers | Inter tabular, medium | `ARC-13` — a clock whose digits shift width is unreadable at a glance |

**Five India-specific rules that are wrong in most imported products:**

1. **Money is `₹`, grouped Indian-style.** `₹12,45,678` — lakh and crore
   grouping, not `₹1,245,678`. Large figures may be written `₹12.46 L` or
   `₹1.25 Cr` in dashboards, never in an invoice.
2. **Dates are `DD-MMM-YYYY`** (`21-Sep-2026`) or `DD/MM/YYYY`. **⚠️ `MM/DD`
   is forbidden everywhere** — it is an actual clinical-safety hazard in a
   product used by staff who read `03/04` as 3 April.
3. **Times are 24-hour** in every clinical context. `14:30`, never `2:30 PM`.
   Clinical timestamps carry a timezone only where cross-facility (IST
   throughout, but stroke clocks state it explicitly).
4. **Names are stored and displayed in Latin *and* native script.** Indian names
   transliterate inconsistently; a patient who registered as "Lakshmanan" and
   returns as "Laxmanan" is the single largest source of duplicate records. See
   `AI-602`.
5. **Weights, heights and doses always carry their unit**, and paediatric doses
   are always per-kg with the weight and its capture time shown beside them.

**Patient-facing documents are bilingual** — English plus the patient's
preferred language — for the discharge summary, prescription, consent and
estimate. That is four print artefacts that must be designed twice (§5.8).

### §5.5 Iconography

One 24px outline set, 2px stroke, plus a 16px variant for dense tables. Rules:

- **`◆` is reserved for AI, at 12px, in AI-indigo.** It appears nowhere else,
  and it is the single strongest "AI everywhere" signal in a screenshot.
- Every clinical-status icon is paired with text (§5.3).
- Icon-only buttons carry a tooltip **and** an accessible name; `P-29`'s and
  `P-33`'s screens never use icon-only controls for a primary action.
- `⚠️` in this document marks a hazard for the *reader*; in the product, hazards
  use the critical palette plus an explicit label.

**`C-41` is the most-reused component in the product** and deserves its
specification here rather than in a screen. Three buttons — `Accept`, `Edit`,
`Reject` — as a real button group, tab-reachable, `Enter` accepts, `Esc` leaves
the draft untouched. `Reject` opens the fixed 5-reason dialog (§4.6). The group
shows the confidence band (`C-44`) and a `Why?` link to `C-42`. It never
collapses into an overflow menu, because a hidden reject control is how AI
output gets accepted by default.

**Reserved:** `C-50` … `C-60`.

### §5.7 Motion & feedback

- Transitions 150–200ms, ease-out. Nothing on a clinical screen animates for
  longer than 200ms.
- **⚠️ No motion on `ARC-12` command walls** beyond a value change — a wall in
  peripheral vision must not attract attention unless something happened.
- A new critical alert does **not** steal focus. It announces via `aria-live`
  and is `role="status"`. Stealing focus mid-dictation or mid-dose-entry is a
  safety hazard.
- Every destructive or irreversible action has an explicit confirmation naming
  what will happen. `Sign` is irreversible and says so.
- Autosave every 20s on any authoring screen, with a visible timestamp. Typed
  clinical content is never lost to a navigation or a network failure.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: all transitions become instant.

### §5.8 Print & label artefacts

Physical output is not an afterthought in an Indian hospital — it is how most
patients receive their record, and several artefacts are statutory.

| Artefact | Size | Must carry | Screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patient wristband | 25 × 280mm | UHID barcode, name, age/sex, ward-bed, allergy flag, MLC flag | `S-04-08` |
| Specimen label | 25 × 50mm | Accession barcode, UHID, name, test, collection datetime, collector | `S-14-02` |
| Prescription | A5 | Hospital + HPR ID of prescriber, reg. no., patient, drugs with generic names, **bilingual instructions** | `S-06-07` |
| Invoice / bill | A4 | GSTIN, HSN/SAC per line, IRN + QR, payer, ward class, non-payables marked | `S-19-06` |
| Estimate letter | A4 | Itemised estimate, scheme applicability, validity, **statutory rate display** | `S-19-04` |
| Discharge summary | A4, 2–4pp | NABH minimum content set, diagnosis with codes, medications, follow-up, signature + reg. no., **bilingual** | `S-13-02` |
| Consent form | A4 | Procedure, risks, alternatives, signature or **thumb impression + witness**, bilingual | `S-02-07` |
| Lab / radiology report | A4 | Result + reference range, method, validator + reg. no., NABL mark where applicable | `S-14-09`, `S-15-05` |
| Attendant pass | 54 × 86mm | Photo, patient, ward, validity, return obligation | `S-04-09` |
| Token slip | 80mm roll | Token number, department, doctor, estimated time | `S-05-03` |

**⚠️ Thumb impression plus witness is a first-class signature mode**, not a
fallback. A meaningful share of patients cannot sign, and a consent flow that
assumes literacy is both exclusionary and legally defective. `C-18` supports
draw, Aadhaar eSign, DSC and thumb-impression-with-witness as peers.

## §6 Global patterns

17 patterns that appear on many screens. Specified once here; a screen spec
names the pattern and its deviations only. **`GP-17` is the only pattern that
appears on every screen without exception.**

| ID | Pattern | Appears on | Key behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GP-01` | App bar (`Z1`) | All | Facility switcher, global search, notification bell, language, user menu |
| `GP-02` | Nav rail (`Z2`) | All but kiosk & wall | Module-level navigation, scoped to the user's capabilities — **a module the user cannot enter is absent, not disabled** |
| `GP-03` | Global search | All | Patient, order, invoice, drug, staff. `AI-901` natural-language mode. Keyboard `/` |
| `GP-04` | Notification bell & centre | All | `NTF-01` … `NTF-32`; criticality-tiered; **⚠️ never carries PHI in an out-of-app channel** |
| `GP-05` | Patient context banner (`Z3`) | ~150 | UHID, name, age/sex, ward-bed, consultant, LOS, payer, **allergy flag**, MLC flag, ABHA chip, optional risk strip |
| `GP-06` | Task inbox | Clinical & ops | One queue per persona; the counterpart to notifications for things that must be *done* |
| `GP-07` | Facility / tenant switcher | All | Explicit, always visible. **⚠️ Switching facility changes authorization scope and must be unmistakable** |
| `GP-08` | Language switcher | All | Per-user; patient-facing documents follow the *patient's* preference, not the user's |
| `GP-09` | Consent & ABHA chip | Patient-scoped | States `Linked` / `Not linked` / `Consent pending` / `Revoked`; click → `S-02-07` |
| `GP-10` | Audit & break-glass banner | Patient-scoped | Amber, full width, reason-before-render; "This access is logged and reviewed" |
| `GP-11` | Break-glass request | Patient-scoped | `S-02-05` modal; reason mandatory; proceeds rather than refusing (§3.2) |
| `GP-12` | Offline strip | All | What works, what is queued, what is blocked, and a pending-sync count |
| `GP-13` | AI assistant launcher | All | `AIP-04` side panel, capability-scoped; declines out-of-scope requests explicitly |
| `GP-14` | Barcode / QR scan | Clinical & ops | Scan-first, **keyed fallback never removed** — scanners fail and labels smudge |
| `GP-15` | Print / export | Most | Every export is a class-3 audit event (§4.9) |
| `GP-16` | Help & guided tour | All | Contextual, per screen; `P-29` and `P-33` get illustrated rather than textual help |
| `GP-17` | ⚠️ **Assistant bubble (`Z7b`)** | **Every screen** | A 56px floating bubble, bottom-right, on every screen. Tapping it opens that portal's assistant (`M-28`) as a `Z8` panel, pre-scoped to the screen and the persona. See §6.1 |

**Notification criticality tiers** (`GP-04`), because a flat notification list
trains people to ignore it:

| Tier | Delivery | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `critical` | Interrupt + page + escalate if unacknowledged | Critical lab value, code stroke, hard-stop override |
| `urgent` | Push + badge, escalates after a stated interval | Pre-auth query expiring, TPA discharge approval received |
| `routine` | Badge only | Result available, appointment booked |
| `digest` | Batched daily | Indicator summaries, expiry warnings |

**⚠️ The PHI rule on outbound channels.** An SMS or WhatsApp message says *"You
have an appointment tomorrow at 14:30"* — never the reason for the visit, the
diagnosis or a result. The notification is **a pointer back into the
authenticated app, not a PHI transport.** This carries the existing corpus's
constraint unchanged and it binds every `NTF-` type.

### §6.1 `GP-17` — the assistant bubble, specified once

**⚠️ This is the only element that appears on every screen in the product**, so
it is specified here in full and **never re-specified in a screen block**. A
screen's spec carries exactly one line about it: `Z7b — GP-17, no deviation`, or
it names its deviation.

> **⚠️ Status: the retrieval model is hypothetical.** The RAG backend, its
> content corpus and its answer quality are **not designed here** and are later
> work (`OQ-539`, `OQ-540`). What this document specifies — and what the mockup
> must show — is the **affordance and the surface**: a bubble on every screen,
> and a per-portal assistant screen behind it (`M-28`). Treat every example
> answer in `M-28` as **illustrative copy for a mockup**, not a committed
> capability.

**What it is.** A 56px floating bubble, bottom-right, carrying the `◆` glyph. It
is the single entry point to that portal's assistant. It does **not** occupy a
bar, a strip or any layout width — it floats above `Z7a`, so it costs no vertical
space on any screen.

```text
                                                       +-----------------+
                                                       | Z8  ASSISTANT   |
+-------------------------------------------------+    |  <>  Clinician  |
| Z7a  [ Save draft ]        [ Sign & publish ]   |    |-----------------|
+-------------------------------------------------+    | you: how do I   |
                                        ( <> )  <--Z7b |  add an addendum|
                                         56px          |-----------------|
                                                       | A signed note   |
   collapsed: a bubble, nothing else                   | cannot be edited|
   tap / press "?" to open the Z8 panel                | -- use Addendum |
                                                       | [1] CMP-NABH-10 |
                                                       | [2] S-08-04 spec|
                                                       |-----------------|
                                                       | [ ask ......  ] |
                                                       +-----------------+
```

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Component | `C-49` bubble · opens `C-32` drawer + `C-42` citations |
| Capability | `AI-911` contextual help, composed with the portal's own capabilities (`M-28`) |
| Pattern / gate | `AIP-04` side panel · **`G1`** · confidence 3-band |
| Explainability | ⚠️ **Mandatory and always visible** — an uncited answer is not rendered at all |
| Keyboard | `?` opens from anywhere · `Esc` closes and leaves the page state untouched |
| Placement | ⚠️ Bottom-right, 24px inset, above `Z7a`. **Never covers a primary action**, never overlaps `Z3`, and shifts up when a `C-33` toast is present |
| Badge | An unread proactive nudge shows a dot; ⚠️ the bubble **never auto-opens** |

**⚠️ Six guardrails. These are why this is safe to put on every screen, and they
are not negotiable per module.**

1. **It is not a clinical adviser.** A clinical question — "is this dose safe",
   "what does this result mean", "should I thrombolyse" — is **declined and
   routed** to the capability that owns it under its own gate: `AI-203`
   differentials, `AI-205` interactions, `AI-705` patient explanation. The
   assistant never answers it directly, at any confidence.
2. **Grounded or silent.** Answers come only from retrieved, cited content. With
   nothing relevant retrieved it shows `AI-ABSTAIN` — *"I don't have
   documentation for that"* plus the support route. ⚠️ **It never extrapolates a
   policy the hospital has not written.**
3. **Capability-scoped.** Retrieval is filtered to what the caller may already
   read. An answer quoting a policy or a record the user could not open through
   the UI is a privilege escalation with a friendly interface — the same rule as
   `AI-902`.
4. **No PHI it did not already have.** In a staff portal it may discuss the
   patient already in context (`Z3`); it may **never** surface a patient the
   user has not opened. In the patient portal it is scoped to `self` only.
5. **Every answer is citable and reportable.** Citations click through to source;
   `Report wrong answer` is always present and feeds `S-25-07`.
6. **It is never the only path.** `AI-OFF` hides the bubble entirely (**not
   greyed**, §1.5) and `GP-16` static help plus a support contact remain.
   ⚠️ **No task anywhere in the product may require the assistant to complete.**

**States** — the three AI states from §1.5 apply to `Z7b` on every screen:
`AI-OFF` bubble hidden, `GP-16` remains · `AI-ABSTAIN` "no documentation for
that" + support route · `AI-LOW` answer behind "low confidence — verify against
the SOP".

**Responsive.** ≥1024px: 56px bubble, 24px inset; panel 420px right drawer.
768–1023px: 48px bubble; panel a 70%-height bottom sheet. <768px: 48px bubble
raised above any bottom nav; panel a full-screen sheet. ⚠️ On `ARC-12` command
walls it is **absent entirely** — a wall has no operator at it (§10.1).

**India & compliance.** `CMP-DPDP-01` — assistant queries are a named processing
purpose. `CMP-DPDP-02` — it answers in the user's `GP-08` language. Corpus and
model hosting obey residency (§2.1 A7, `S-25-06`).

**Where the conversation lives.** The bubble is the *affordance*; the
*conversation* is `M-28`, which defines one assistant screen per portal with its
own scope, its own permitted question classes and its own refusal behaviour.

## §7 India-first & compliance overlay

63 obligations. **Each row names a UI consequence**, because a compliance
requirement that does not change a screen does not belong in a mockup brief. The
design principle is `DD-009`: **India is the default regulatory pack, not a
feature flag** — and §7.10 is what makes the product sellable outside India
without rewriting it.

Families: `ABDM` digital health · `PMJAY` scheme · `TPA` cashless insurance ·
`NABH` accreditation · `GST` tax · `DPDP` data protection · `DRUG` pharmacy &
controlled substances · `DIAG` diagnostics regulation · `STAT` statutory
reporting · `INTL` international readiness.

### §7.1 ABDM / ABHA / consent (7)

| ID | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-ABDM-01` | ABHA number or address linked to the patient record | `abha` field type; `GP-09` chip with four states | `S-04-03`, `S-04-07` |
| `CMP-ABDM-02` | Care-context linking requires a consent artefact | Chip states `Consent pending`; PHI paths gated on it | `S-02-07`, `GP-09` |
| `CMP-ABDM-03` | HIP publish of 5 record types — OPConsultation, DiagnosticReport, Prescription, DischargeSummary, ImmunizationRecord | **Per-record-type publish status**, not one global flag | `S-03-07`, `S-13-02` |
| `CMP-ABDM-04` | Publish failures must be visible and retryable | A dedicated failure queue with reason classification | `S-03-07` |
| `CMP-ABDM-05` | HIE-CM consent honoured mid-fetch, including revocation | Fetch aborts on revocation; partial data is discarded, not shown | `S-02-08` |
| `CMP-ABDM-06` | Scan & Share QR token issued without typing | Kiosk QR screen; front office shows an `arrived via Scan & Share` state | `S-04-02`, `S-05-03` |
| `CMP-ABDM-07` | HPR ID on every clinician; HFR ID per facility | HPR ID printed on every prescription (`⚠️` mandatory for teleconsults) | `S-01-02`, `S-06-07` |

| ID | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-PMJAY-01` | Beneficiary verification before package selection | Verify step **blocks** package selection until resolved | `S-20-02` |
| `CMP-PMJAY-02` | HBP package code drives the entitlement | Package selector with HBP code, specialty, implant add-ons | `S-20-02` |
| `CMP-PMJAY-03` | ⚠️ Package rate fixes the permitted bed class | Bed-class options **above entitlement are disabled with an inline reason** — `AI-611` may not rank around this | `S-08-02`, `S-08-05` |
| `CMP-PMJAY-04` | Blocking request, query response, claim submission (TMS) | Distinct states, each with its own SLA clock | `S-20-04`, `S-20-06` |

| `CMP-PMJAY-06` | CGHS / ECHS / ESI referral or permission letter captured | Letter upload + validity; ESIC IP number validated | `S-20-01` |

| ID | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-TPA-01` | Pre-auth pack assembled from the clinical record | Builder showing what is present, missing and auto-assembled | `S-20-04` |

### §7.4 NABH accreditation (11)

NABH 5th edition. **Every clinical module contributes evidence**; `M-24` owns
the standard-to-evidence map. The obligations below are the ones that change a
screen rather than a policy document.

| ID | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-NABH-01` | Initial assessment within 24h of admission | Countdown chip on the worklist row; overdue = ⚠️ | `S-08-03`, `S-08-07` |
| `CMP-NABH-02` | Nursing reassessment at defined intervals | Due/overdue state per patient per shift | `S-10-01`, `S-10-06` |
| `CMP-NABH-03` | Care plan documented and countersigned | Co-sign state visible; unsigned plans surface in a queue | `S-10-06`, `S-06-09` |
| `CMP-NABH-04` | Discharge summary minimum content set | **Sign is blocked until the minimum set is complete**, with the gaps named | `S-13-02` |
| `CMP-NABH-05` | Medication orders legible, complete, no banned abbreviations | `AI-114` check on blur; banned abbreviations rejected | `S-06-07`, `S-09-01` |
| `CMP-NABH-06` | High-risk medication double-check | `G4` dual-signoff on the designated list | `S-10-03` |
| `CMP-NABH-07` | Surgical safety checklist completed for every procedure | `ARC-14` runner; **the OT record cannot close without it** | `S-11-04` |
| `CMP-NABH-08` | Informed consent before every defined procedure | Consent state on the pre-op checklist; blocks scheduling confirmation | `S-02-07`, `S-11-04` |
| `CMP-NABH-09` | Incident reporting, RCA and corrective-action tracking | `ARC-03` wizard; CAPA items with owners and due dates | `S-24-03` |
| `CMP-NABH-10` | ⚠️ A signed record is never edited — only amended | `amend` verb only; `LOCKED` state with an Addendum action | §3.2, all authoring screens |
| `CMP-NABH-11` | Every clinical entry carries author identity, registration number, date and time | Attestation block on every authoring screen; stamped on sign, never typed | All authoring screens, §5.8 |

**Also NABH-driven but owned elsewhere:** ~35 quality indicators (`S-24-01`),
2%/month medical-record audit (`S-24-06`), credentialing files (`S-23-05`), mock
drills (`S-23-10`), committee minutes (`S-24-01`).

| `CMP-DIAG-01` | ⚠️ PCPNDT Form F before any obstetric ultrasound report is released | **Form F cannot be bypassed.** No report releases without it; machine registration and monthly register | `S-15-07` |
| `CMP-DIAG-02` | AERB / eLORA equipment registration, RSO record, TLD badge cycle | Dose register, badge issue/read cycle | `S-15-08` |
| `CMP-DIAG-03` | NABL — IQC, EQAS, calibration, competency, method validation | QC screens as records; TAT indicators | `S-14-08`, `S-14-10` |
| `CMP-DIAG-04` | Blood bank licence, e-Raktkosh, mandatory TTI panel, donor deferral | Donor deferral register; component stock; mandatory test panel enforced | `S-17-01`, `S-17-02` |
| `CMP-DIAG-05` | ⚠️ HIV Act 2017 — consent before test, restricted result visibility | Result visibility restricted by capability; consent gate before ordering | `S-14-05`, `S-02-07` |

### §7.9 Statutory reporting & medico-legal (7)

| ID | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-STAT-01` | ⚠️ MLC registration, police intimation with acknowledgement, wound certificate | MLC number; intimation memo with acknowledgement capture; court-summons tracker | `S-04-10`, `S-07-08`, `S-24-09` |
| `CMP-STAT-02` | Notifiable diseases (IDSP / IHIP) | `AI-809` auto-detects from diagnosis or lab result → notification form → receipt | `S-24-10` |
| `CMP-STAT-03` | Birth & death registration (CRS), MCCD Form 4 / 4A | Form generation, cause-of-death coding, municipal submission | `S-13-06` |
| `CMP-STAT-04` | Biomedical Waste Rules 2016 — category-wise daily weight, CBWTF manifest, CPCB annual return | Daily log; handover manifest | `S-22-06` |
| `CMP-STAT-05` | Unidentified patient and unclaimed body process | Identity-pending state that does not block care; police handover documentation | `S-07-07`, `S-13-06` |
| `CMP-STAT-06` | Statutory licences — fire NOC, PCB consent, lift, boiler, CEA registration | Licence register with renewal escalation | `S-22-07`, `S-01-02` |
| `CMP-STAT-07` | PF / ESI / PT / TDS / gratuity computation and challans | Statutory computation, challan generation, Form 16 | `S-23-09` |

### §7.10 International readiness (4)

This is what makes `DD-009` real rather than a slide. The four hooks below are
the entire mechanism by which the product leaves India.

| ID | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-INTL-01` | Regulatory pack is selectable per facility | **A single configuration screen** switches the statutory set, the date/money format, the terminology bindings and the required-field profile | `S-01-06` |
| `CMP-INTL-02` | FHIR R4 as the external clinical contract; HL7 v2 for legacy ADT/ORU/ORM | Interface monitor is standard-agnostic; message trace shows either | `S-03-05`, `S-03-06` |
| `CMP-INTL-03` | Terminology bindings are configuration, not code — ICD-10 / ICD-11 / SNOMED CT / LOINC / NAMASTE | Per-field binding point; a pack change re-binds without a release | `S-03-01`, `S-03-02` |
| `CMP-INTL-04` | DICOM for imaging; measurement units and paper sizes per pack | A4 vs Letter, kg vs lb, °C vs °F all follow the pack | `S-15-03`, §5.8 |

**⚠️ The one thing `CMP-INTL-01` cannot switch** is a clinical-safety rule
expressed in the UI, such as the `MM/DD` prohibition (§5.4). Date-format
ambiguity is a hazard in every jurisdiction, so `DD-MMM-YYYY` remains the
default everywhere and `MM/DD` is never selected by a pack.

## §8 Sample data kit

**Mandatory, and this is the rule that makes the deck read as one product.**
Every mockup uses this cast and only this cast. Without it, 27 mockups show 27
different patients with inconsistent ID formats, American names and dollar
amounts — which is the single most common way a hospital demo falls apart.

### §8.6 The rule

**Never invent data outside this kit.** If a mockup needs a value the kit does
not have, add it here first and tell the other designers. A new patient name
invented for one screen is a defect, not a detail — it is the thing a client
notices and cannot un-notice.

Fixed reference moment for every mockup: **Monday 21 September 2026, 08:40
IST**, at facility `SD-F-01` unless the screen is explicitly a spoke or a
patient-facing screen. A consistent clock is what makes 27 screenshots look like
one working day rather than 27 unrelated captures.

## §9 Master screen registry

**This is the designer's real table of contents.** All 256 screens, every ID
allocated, grouped by layer. `ARC` names the archetype the screen inherits from
(§10.1) — the screen's specification states only its *deltas* from that
archetype, which is the mechanism that makes full depth affordable. `AI` lists
the capability IDs that surface on the screen; every screen has at least one,
which is the "AI in every module" guarantee made checkable.

Column meanings: **Route** is a client-side UI route, not an API endpoint
(§0.2) · **Persona** lists primary personas only; the module's `M-xx.2` table is
authoritative · **Tier** per §1.7 · **Status** per §1.1.

## §10 Screen archetypes & mockup production plan

### §10.1 Screen archetype library

**This is the mechanism that makes full depth affordable.** Each archetype is
specified **once** — layout skeleton, canonical workflow, states, keyboard model
and AI slots. Each of the 256 screens then declares its archetype and states only
its **deltas**. A screen therefore *inherits a complete specification* rather
than having none, which is how depth survives breadth.

Ordered by usage, which is also the recommended build order — `ARC-15` and
`ARC-01` together account for 75 of 256 screens, so getting those two right is
worth more than the other 26 combined.
