|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-27` Store / Materials Manager | Stock, indents, GRN, PO, vendors, expiry | `S-21-01`…`S-21-06` | `facility`, `stock.write` | Compact | Desktop + scanner |
| `P-28` Biomedical Engineer | Assets, maintenance, calibration, breakdowns | `S-21-07`…`S-21-09` | `facility`, `asset.write` | Compact | Tablet + scanner, field |
| `P-08` Nurse-in-Charge | Ward indents | — | `unit` | Compact | Nursing station |
| `P-14` Pharmacist | Drug expiry and recall (shared view) | — | `facility` | Compact | Counter |
| `P-02` Administrator | Approves purchase above threshold | — | `facility.admin` | Comfortable | Desktop |

### M-21.5 AI capabilities in this module

| `AI-621` | Expiry, wastage & recall exposure prediction | `S-21-01`, `S-21-06` | `AIP-06`, `AIP-07` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ FEFO and the expiry rule itself are deterministic |
| `AI-113` | Document intelligence — OCR of invoices & certificates | `S-21-03` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | Reads supplier invoices and batch certificates; human confirms |
| `AI-504` | Rate contract & price comparison | `S-21-05` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Contracted rate is a deterministic lookup |
| `AI-622` | Equipment failure prediction | `S-21-07`…`S-21-09` | `AIP-06`, `AIP-05` | G1 | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **Scheduled preventive maintenance remains.** A prediction never cancels a statutory calibration |
| `AI-813` | Licence & calibration expiry prediction | `S-21-08` | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | Statutory dates are deterministic |

**Module AI narrative.** *"The system tells you which ₹12 lakh of stock will
expire before you use it, ranked by what you can still return or redeploy. And
it watches your ventilators' usage hours and fault history — so the one that is
about to fail gets serviced before the night it is needed, not on the calendar
date three months later."*

## M-22 · Support Services

**In one line.** Dietary, housekeeping, CSSD, laundry, ambulance, facilities and
waste.

### M-22.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** Seven support functions that keep a hospital running and are
routinely absent from EMR products: the diet order board and kitchen indent, the
housekeeping task board, CSSD sterilisation cycles and tracking, linen and
laundry circulation, ambulance fleet and dispatch, the biomedical waste log and
manifest, the facility statutory licence register, and porter/patient-transport
requests.

**Does NOT cover.** The clinical **diet order** is `M-17`; this module owns
production and delivery. Bed *turnaround state* is `M-08`; this module owns the
housekeeping **task**. Pre-hospital stroke care is `M-18`; this module owns the
fleet.

**⚠️ `P-29` the housekeeping supervisor may have limited English literacy.**
Their screens are icon-and-colour first with regional-language text as
reinforcement — which is a *different* design, not a simplified one (§3.3).
Getting this wrong means the task board is not used, and an unused task board
means bed turnaround is still managed by phone.

**What the client will judge this module on.** Bed turnaround time, and whether
biomedical-waste and statutory-licence evidence is producible for an inspection
without a scramble — because `CMP-STAT-04` and `CMP-STAT-06` failures close
services.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-29` Housekeeping Supervisor | Tasks, laundry, waste, transport | `S-22-02`, `S-22-04`, `S-22-06`, `S-22-08` | `unit` | Comfortable | ⚠️ Phone, icon-first |
| `P-20` Dietitian | Diet board and kitchen indent | `S-22-01` | `facility` | Comfortable | Tablet |

their own language, with pictures. And your biomedical-waste log builds itself
from what the wards actually disposed of, so the CPBC return is a print rather
than a reconstruction."*

## M-23 · HR, Rostering, Payroll & Credentialing

**In one line.** The workforce — hired, privileged, rostered, paid and
compliant.

### M-23.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** The HR home and workforce dashboard, the duty roster planner, the
employee directory and profile, recruitment and onboarding, **clinical
credentialing and privileging**, licence/registration/expiry tracking, attendance
and shift actuals, leave management, the payroll run with statutory computation,
training/competency/mock drills, and performance with attrition risk.

**Does NOT cover.** Clinician *identity* and their role records are `M-02` — an
employee is a `Party` like everyone else, and there is **no separate doctor
record** (`DEC-006` H-7, §E). Consultant revenue share is `M-19`. Clinician
*session templates* are `M-05`. Payroll **disbursement** is external; this module
produces the instruction.

**⚠️ The dependency that makes this module load-bearing for safety.**
Credentialing and privileging are HR facts with an **authorization
consequence**: a lapsed licence or an expired privilege must withdraw the
corresponding capability at request time. `M-02` reads that from here (§2.6
declared exception, `DEC-004` F-16). A hospital where an unprivileged surgeon can
book a case has an HR problem that presents as a patient-safety incident.

**What the client will judge this module on.** The roster. A 1,400-bed group
rosters several thousand staff across four sites with skill-mix, statutory
rest, leave and licence constraints — and most do it in spreadsheets.
`S-23-02` finding tomorrow's coverage gaps before they happen is the pitch.

### M-23.2 Personas & permissions

| Persona | What they do here | Owns screens | Scope | Density | Device |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-30` HR Manager | Directory, recruitment, attendance, leave, training, performance | `S-23-01`, `S-23-03`, `S-23-04`, `S-23-07`, `S-23-08`, `S-23-10`, `S-23-11` | `group`, `hr.write` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-31` Payroll Officer | Payroll run and statutory computation | `S-23-09` | `facility`, `payroll.write` | Compact | Desktop |
| `P-32` Credentialing Officer | Credentialing, privileging, licences | `S-23-05`, `S-23-06` | `group`, `credential.write` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-08` Nurse-in-Charge | Ward roster and shift actuals | `S-23-02` | `unit` | Compact | Nursing station |
| `P-02` Administrator | Approves privileging; reads workforce | — | `facility.admin` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-25` Quality Manager | Training, competency, mock drills | — | `facility` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| All staff | Own profile and leave | — | `self` | Comfortable | Phone |

⚠️ `hr.write` confers **no clinical read**. And `payroll.write` is scoped
per-facility deliberately — a group-wide payroll capability is a concentration of
risk with no operational justification.

### M-23.5 AI capabilities in this module

| AI | Capability | Surfaces on | Pattern | Gate | Explain | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI-623` | Roster optimisation & coverage-gap detection | `S-23-01`, `S-23-02`, `S-23-07`, `S-23-08` | `AIP-03`, `AIP-05` | **G2** | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **Statutory rest, skill mix and privileging are hard constraints.** AI optimises *within* them and may never roster an unprivileged or under-rested person |
| `AI-624` | Attrition risk & staffing demand forecast | `S-23-01`, `S-23-04`, `S-23-11` | `AIP-06` | G1 | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **Never used in a disciplinary, appraisal or termination decision.** Informs recruitment planning only |
| `AI-907` | Master-data deduplication | `S-23-03` | `AIP-03` | G2 | Mandatory | Manual dedup remains |
| `AI-113` | Document intelligence — OCR of certificates & CVs | `S-23-04` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | Reads degrees, registrations, experience letters; human confirms every field |
| `AI-814` | Credentialing & privileging gap detection | `S-23-05` | `AIP-05`, `AIP-07` | G2 | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **The privilege decision is a human committee act.** AI finds missing documents and expiries |
| `AI-813` | Licence & registration expiry prediction | `S-23-06` | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ The statutory expiry date itself is deterministic |
| `AI-517` | Payroll & attendance anomaly detection | `S-23-07`, `S-23-09` | `AIP-05`, `AIP-07` | G1 | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ Statutory computation (PF, ESI, PT, TDS, gratuity) is **deterministic**; AI flags outliers only |
| `AI-816` | Training & competency gap detection | `S-23-10` | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | Manual training matrix remains |

**⚠️ `AI-624`'s guardrail is the one an employee-relations lawyer will ask
about.** An attrition-risk score used in an appraisal or a termination is both
unfair and legally exposed. It is permitted for **recruitment and capacity
planning only**, it is not visible on an individual's appraisal screen, and
`S-23-11` states that boundary on the screen.

**Module AI narrative.** *"Tomorrow night's roster has a gap: the only nurse
rostered to ICU-1 whose paediatric competency is current is on leave. The system
found it today and proposed three people who are privileged, rested and
available. It will never propose someone whose licence lapsed last week — that is
a hard rule, not a preference."*

## M-24 · Quality, NABH, Infection Control, MRD & Medico-Legal

**In one line.** Evidence an auditor will accept, produced as a by-product of
care.

### M-24.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** The quality dashboard and indicators, the NABH standard and evidence
explorer, incident reporting and RCA, HAI surveillance, antibiogram and
resistance trends, medical-record audit and completeness, MRD coding and
case-mix, record retention and disposition, the medico-legal register and court
summons tracker, and statutory/notifiable-disease reporting. It also owns the
**audit log's read path**.

**Does NOT cover.** Clinical care itself. Every clinical module *contributes*
evidence; this module **maps, audits and produces** it. Claim coding is `M-20`;
the coding *discipline* and case-mix are here.

**⚠️ The audit read path has a specific and deliberate shape.** It exists
(`DEC-008` J-12 requires it), reading it is itself an auditable event, and
**no fact obtained from it may enter an authorization decision at any layer**
(`DEC-009` K-7). A return path from audit into authority would reconstruct the
relationship-existence oracle that §3.2's uniform-refusal rule prevents. So the
read path is reachable from this module and from **no request-handling path**.

**What the client will judge this module on.** `S-24-02`. A NABH surveyor asks
"show me evidence for AAC.3" and the answer is four clicks — the standard, its
objective elements, the evidence each is satisfied by, and a click through to the
actual records. For an NABH-aspiring group (§2.1 A4) that is the difference
between a six-week preparation scramble and a Tuesday afternoon.

### M-24.2 Personas & permissions

| Persona | What they do here | Owns screens | Scope | Density | Device |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-25` Quality Manager / NABH Coordinator | Indicators, NABH map, incidents, audits | `S-24-01`…`S-24-03`, `S-24-06` | `group`, `quality.write` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-26` Infection Control Nurse | HAI surveillance, antibiogram, isolation | `S-24-04`, `S-24-05` | `facility` | Comfortable | Tablet, ward rounds |
| `P-24` MRD Officer / Coder | Coding, case-mix, retention, medico-legal | `S-24-07`…`S-24-10` | `facility`, `mrd.write` | Compact | MRD |
| `P-43` Data Protection Officer | Retention, disposition, rights conflicts | — | `group`, `dpo.read` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-02` Administrator | Reads indicators and committee packs | — | `facility` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-45` Auditor / Regulator (external) | ⚠️ Read-only, time-boxed, fully logged | — | ⚠️ Enumerated, expiring | Comfortable | Desktop |

⚠️ `P-45` is the only **external** persona with access to clinical evidence. The
grant is enumerated by screen, time-boxed, and every access is a class-3 audit
event. `S-24-02` is designed so that an inspection is answerable without handing
over broader access.

**⚠️ `S-24-08` surfaces a genuine legal conflict rather than resolving it
silently.** A DPDP erasure request (`CMP-DPDP-03`) collides with statutory
medical-record retention — MRD 3 years, MLC 10 years, PCPNDT 2 years. `DD-013`
decides that the conflict is **shown**, the refusal **states which obligation
overrides**, and the decision is recorded. A product that silently honours
erasure destroys defensible records; one that silently refuses breaches DPDP.

**Module AI narrative.** *"Your NABH evidence map is live. It tells you which
objective elements have evidence, which are thin, and which have nothing — from
the actual records, not from a spreadsheet someone updates before the survey. And
when three patients on the same ward grow the same organism, the system says
'possible outbreak' before your infection-control nurse has finished her
rounds."*

## M-25 · Analytics, Executive Command Centre & AI Governance

**In one line.** What the group is doing, and whether the AI is still working.

### M-25.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** The group executive dashboard, the facility operations command
wall, clinical outcomes and benchmarking, financial and payer-mix analytics, the
natural-language analytics console, and the **AI governance surface** — model
registry and health, override/drift/per-site performance, and patient-facing AI
transparency.

**Does NOT cover.** Operational screens own their own live boards — `S-08-01`,
`S-07-01`, `S-18-01` are not in this module. This module is **cross-facility and
retrospective**, plus the one forward-looking thing nobody else owns: whether the
AI fabric is still performing.

**⚠️ `P-01`'s scope is `group` for roll-ups and never clinical detail.** A CEO
sees occupancy, ALOS, payer mix and denial rate across four hospitals. Drilling
from a roll-up into an individual patient's record requires a care relationship
like anyone else — `group` scope confers aggregate reads, not a master key.

**What the client will judge this module on.** Two things: whether the Monday
morning executive number is the *same* number the facility sees (one definition,
versioned — `AI-802`), and whether `S-25-07` gives an honest answer to "is the AI
still working, and where is it worse?"

### M-25.2 Personas & permissions

| Persona | What they do here | Owns screens | Scope | Density | Device |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-01` Group CEO / Board | Executive roll-ups | `S-25-01` | ⚠️ `group` **aggregate only** | Comfortable | Tablet, phone |
| `P-02` Administrator / Superintendent | Operations wall, outcomes, finance | `S-25-02`…`S-25-04` | `facility`, `group.read` | Comfortable | Desktop + wall |
| `P-25` Quality Manager | Outcomes, AI override and drift review | `S-25-07` | `group`, `quality.read` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-42` IT Administrator | Model registry, kill switches, enablement | `S-25-06` | `group`, `ai.admin` | Compact | Desktop |
| `P-43` Data Protection Officer | AI transparency and disclosure | `S-25-08` | `group`, `dpo.read` | Comfortable | Desktop |
| `P-21` Billing Executive | Financial analytics | — | `facility` | Compact | Desktop |
| `P-09` Bed Manager | Operations wall | — | `facility` | Compact | Wall |

| `AI-909` | Model health, drift & per-site performance | `S-25-06`, `S-25-07` | `AIP-06`, `AIP-05` | G1 | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **⊘ no fallback** — its unavailability triggers the global kill switch (§4.8) |
| `AI-910` | AI transparency & disclosure register | `S-25-08` | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | Static disclosure document remains |

**⚠️ `AI-902`'s guardrail is the one that makes NL analytics safe.** A
natural-language question is answered **within the caller's existing
capabilities**, and the console shows the query it actually ran. An NL layer that
can answer questions the user could not have asked through the UI is a privilege
escalation with a friendly interface.

**Module AI narrative.** *"Your CEO asks 'why did Nashik's denial rate double
last month' in plain English and gets the answer with the query it ran, so
someone can check it. And one screen tells you whether every AI capability in
the product is still performing — per hospital, because a model that works in
Bengaluru may not work in Kolhapur."*

### M-25.6 India & compliance overlay

| CMP | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-DPDP-01` | Purpose registry and lawful basis | ⚠️ **AI processing purposes named explicitly** | `S-25-08` |
| `CMP-DPDP-05` | Breach assessment within 72 hours | Breach clock visible to the DPO | `S-25-08` |
| `CMP-NABH-01`…`11` | Indicator contribution | Indicators roll up from `M-24` with one definition | `S-25-01`, `S-25-03` |
| `CMP-GST-01` | Tax reporting inputs | Payer-mix and tax analytics | `S-25-04` |
| `CMP-INTL-01` | Regulatory pack per facility | Cross-facility roll-ups must not mix incompatible definitions | `S-25-01` |

**⚠️ One India-specific constraint on the AI itself.** Data residency (§2.1 A7)
constrains every model and vendor choice, and CDSCO software-as-medical-device
classification applies to several `AI-2xx` and `AI-4xx` capabilities.
`S-25-06` therefore records, per capability: model, version, hosting region,
residency guarantee and SaMD classification. That is not decoration — it is what
an inspection will ask for.

### M-25.7 Integration touchpoints

| System | Dir | Standard | UI consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every module | **←** | Internal | Metrics and events; this module writes nothing operational |
| AI fabric | **↔** | Internal | Kill switches out; health and drift telemetry in |
| Group BI / warehouse | **→** | File / API | Export for external reporting |
| `M-24` audit | **←** | Internal | ⚠️ Read path only, itself audited |
| Model vendors | **←** | Vendor API | Version and performance metadata |

### M-25.8 Key data entities

| Entity | Shown as | Identifier format | Example (§8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indicator | Tile + trend | `{code}/{period}/{scope}` | with versioned definition |
| Model registration | Registry row | `{AI-id}@{version}` | + region, SaMD class |
| Drift observation | Trend point | `{AI-id}/{facility}/{period}` | ⚠️ per site |
| Override record | Review row | `{AI-id}/{disposition}` | §4.6 vocabulary |
| Disclosure entry | Register row | `{AI-id}/{purpose}` | patient-facing text |
| NL query | Console turn | `{user}/{ts}` | with the executed query |

### M-25.10 Screen specifications

#### S-25-01 · Group Executive Dashboard

**One-liner.** The group on a Monday morning.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Route** | `/analytics/executive` |
| **Archetype** | `ARC-20` dashboard · density comfortable |
| **Persona** | `P-01` · `P-02` |
| **Permission** | ⚠️ `group` **aggregate only** for `P-01`. Drilling to a patient requires a care relationship like anyone else. |
| **Entry** | Default landing for `P-01` at sign-in · `GP-02` ▸ Analytics |
| **Exit** | Tile → `S-25-04` / `S-25-02` · ▸ Ask → `S-28-11` · ▸ AI health → `S-25-07` |
| **In workflows** | `W-25-1` s1,2? · `W-28-3` s1 |
| **AI** | ◆AI-802 ◆AI-612 |
| **Tier / status** | T1 · ✅ |

**Zones.** `Z1` `Z2` — `GP-01`, `GP-02`, no deviation · `Z3` — n/a: not patient-scoped · `Z4` — scope selector, period, refresh state · `Z5` — `C-24` tile grid · `Z7b` — `GP-17` assistant bubble, no deviation (§6.1)

**Actions.**

| Action | Placement | Style | Enabled when | On activate | Confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Drill into tile | tile click | primary | `group.read` | ⚠️ reaches **aggregates only** — never patient detail | none |
| Compare facilities | `Z4` | primary | always | the same metric across all four sites | none |
| Ask a question | `Z7b` bubble | secondary | `AI-902` | → `S-28-11` | none |
| View definition | inline | secondary | always | ⚠️ versioned — the same number the facility sees | none |

**AI touchpoints.**

| AI | Capability | Pattern | Gate | Explain | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI-802` | Indicator computation & trend alerting | `AIP-05`, `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ **Definitions are deterministic and versioned** — the same metric means the same thing at every level |
| `AI-612` | Census & occupancy forecast | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | Current census remains |
| `AI-911` | Contextual assistant | `AIP-04` | G1 | ⚠️ Mandatory, cited | §6.1 — never clinical, grounded or silent |

**States.**

| Code | What to draw |
|---|---|
| `LOADING` | `C-45` skeleton matching the loaded geometry; `Z7a` disabled |
| `EMPTY` | explains why it is empty and the action that would change that |
| `PARTIAL` | the failed region names what is missing and since when; the rest stays usable |
| `ERROR` | recoverable, input preserved, retry plus an escape hatch |
| `VALIDATION` | problem count, inline errors, focus to the first, primary stays disabled |
| `DENIED` | `C-36` panel — what is missing, who grants it, request action. ⚠️ **no patient data on screen** |
| `BREAKGLASS` | `GP-10` amber banner, reason before content renders, "logged and reviewed" |
| `OFFLINE` | `C-37` strip — what works, what is queued, what is blocked; typed content never lost |
| `STALE` | timestamp turns amber, "Data as of HH:MM · Refresh" |
| `SAVING` | primary disabled with a spinner; content not locked |
| `LOCKED` | read-only naming who holds it and since when, plus the legitimate next action |
| `AI-OFF` | every `◆` affordance **hidden, not greyed**; the `Z7b` bubble hidden; one quiet line; screen fully usable |
| `AI-ABSTAIN` | states what is missing and the action that would fix it; **never a null or zero score** |
| `AI-LOW` | delivered collapsed with an amber band; acceptance blocked until expanded |

**Responsive.** ≥1440 4 columns · 1024–1439 2 columns · <768 1 column, priority order

**Keyboard.** `Enter` drills into the focused tile · `r` refreshes.

**Accessibility.** Every `◆` region is `role="region"` with the confidence band in its accessible name — never colour alone. · Clinical status carries an icon **and** text (§5.3); abnormal reads `↑ High`, not a red cell. · Contrast ≥4.5:1 in both themes; touch targets ≥44px.

**Sample data.** ⚠️ Four facilities — occupancy 88/74/81/69%, ALOS 4.2d, denial rate 4.1% overall but **8.8% at `SD-F-03`**, DTN median 41 min.

**Drawing notes.** ⚠️ **Deck beat #1, and the deck's opening frame.** Draw four facilities side by side with one off-trend metric highlighted — that is what a CEO looks for in ten seconds. · ⚠️ State that the number is the **same number the facility sees**, with a versioned definition. Executive and operational dashboards disagreeing is the classic failure. · Include the stroke DTN median — the flagship reaching the board's dashboard is the point. · ₹ with lakh and crore grouping.

## M-26 · Patient Portal, Mobile App & Kiosk

**In one line.** What the patient and their family can do without asking anyone.

### M-26.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** The patient app home, appointment booking and management, health
records and reports, the report explainer, bills and UPI payment, symptom intake
and pre-visit questionnaires, medication reminders and adherence, family and
attendant access, the self-service kiosk, and feedback/grievance/NPS.

**Does NOT cover.** Teleconsultation sessions are `M-27`. The ABHA Scan & Share
kiosk at the counter is `M-04` — this module owns the *patient-initiated*
kiosk journey. Booking *engine* and slots are `M-05`; this is the patient's
surface onto them.

**⚠️ The scoping rule this whole module depends on.** A patient's data is scoped
**server-side to the authenticated subject**, never to a client-supplied
identifier. This carries the existing corpus's rule unchanged and it is the
difference between a portal and a data breach.

**⚠️ Design reality for `P-33`.** The primary device is a phone, often a
low-end Android on an intermittent connection, and literacy in English cannot be
assumed. Every patient-facing screen is phone-first, works at 2G, and renders in
the patient's language (§5.4, `GP-08`). A portal designed at 1440px desktop
width will not be used.

**What the client will judge this module on.** Whether patients actually use it
— which in practice means whether the *report explainer* (`S-26-04`) and UPI
payment (`S-26-05`) work well enough to be the reason someone installs the app.

### M-26.2 Personas & permissions

| Persona | What they do here | Owns screens | Scope | Density | Device |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-33` Patient | Everything | `S-26-01`…`S-26-07`, `S-26-09`, `S-26-10` | ⚠️ `self`, server-side | Comfortable | ⚠️ Phone, kiosk, variable literacy |
| `P-34` Patient Attendant / Family | Delegated access | `S-26-08` | ⚠️ `self` of the patient, **by explicit grant only** | Comfortable | Phone |
| `P-03` Front Office | Assists at the kiosk | — | `facility` | Compact | Kiosk-side |

⚠️ `P-34`'s access is an explicit, revocable delegation recorded as a role
record with a period (`DEC-001` D-4, §E) — never an informal share of
credentials, and never inferred from a relationship claimed at the counter.

| Arrive from | Trigger | Lands on | Leaves to |

| App launch | Patient action | `S-26-01` | Anywhere |
| `NTF-05` appointment reminder | Push | `S-26-02` | — |
| `NTF-04` report ready | Push | `S-26-03` | `S-26-04` |
| `NTF-13` bill due | Push | `S-26-05` | UPI / gateway |
| `NTF-15` medication due | Push | `S-26-07` | — |
| Pre-visit, 24h before | Push | `S-26-06` | Feeds `S-06-03` |
| Hospital arrival | Kiosk | `S-26-09` | `S-05-03` token |
| Post-discharge | Push | `S-26-10` | `S-24-03` if a grievance |

### M-26.5 AI capabilities in this module

| AI | Capability | Surfaces on | Pattern | Gate | Explain | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI-701` | App personalisation & next-best-action | `S-26-01` | `AIP-10`, `AIP-06` | G0 | On demand | ⚠️ Static menu remains; never hides a function the patient is entitled to |
| `AI-703` | ⚠️ Conversational patient assistant | `S-26-01`, `S-26-04` | `AIP-04` | **G1** | **Mandatory** — with citations | ⚠️ **Never diagnoses, never advises on treatment, never interprets a result as reassuring.** Escalates to a human; FAQ + "talk to a person" is the fallback |
| `AI-710` | Appointment self-service assist | `S-26-02` | `AIP-03` | G1 | Mandatory | All slots browsable |
| `AI-605` | Slot recommendation | `S-26-02` | `AIP-03` | G1 | Mandatory | — |
| `AI-705` | Report explainer in plain language | `S-26-03`, `S-26-04` | `AIP-01`, `AIP-04` | **G1** | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **The report as issued is always shown first and unaltered.** The explainer is additive, and offers a callback |
| `AI-110` | Translation & transliteration | `S-26-03` | `AIP-02` | G2 | On demand | English fallback with the limitation stated |
| `AI-707` | Payment reminder & UPI nudge | `S-26-05` | `AIP-10` | G0 | — | ⚠️ Never conditions care on payment |
| `AI-704` | Symptom intake & pre-visit questionnaire | `S-26-06` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | ⚠️ **Not triage.** Structures information for the clinician; static questionnaire remains |
| `AI-112` | Structured extraction from free text | `S-26-06` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | — |
| `AI-706` | Medication reminder & adherence nudge | `S-26-07` | `AIP-10`, `AIP-06` | G0 | On demand | Fixed-schedule reminders remain |
| `AI-712` | Family & attendant communication summary | `S-26-08` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Scoped to what the delegation permits |
| `AI-711` | Kiosk guidance & wayfinding | `S-26-09` | `AIP-02`, `AIP-10` | G0 | — | Printed signage remains |
| `AI-709` | Feedback sentiment & grievance routing | `S-26-10` | `AIP-07` | G2 | Mandatory | ⚠️ A grievance is **never** closed by AI; routing only |

**⚠️ `AI-703` and `AI-705` carry the strictest guardrails in the atlas, and for
the same reason.** A patient-facing model that appears to interpret a result is
practising medicine. `S-26-04` shows the issued report **unaltered and first**,
explains terminology beneath it, cites what it drew on, states plainly that it is
not a medical opinion, and offers a callback. That design is what makes the
feature shippable at all.

**Module AI narrative.** *"Your patient gets her report and, underneath it, an
explanation of what 'HbA1c 7.8' actually means — in Kannada, with the original
report untouched above it and a 'talk to someone' button. It never tells her she
is fine. It tells her what the words mean and who to ask."*

### M-26.9 Workflows

#### W-26-1 · Patient receives a report and understands it

**Spine.** `S-26-01 → S-26-03 → S-26-04`
**Deck beat #9.**
**⚠️ The design that makes this shippable.** The issued report is shown
**unaltered and first**; the explainer is additive and never reassures.

| # | Actor | Screen | What happens | AI | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `P-33` | `S-26-01` | S: push notification "report ready" — ⚠️ **no PHI in the notification** | ◆AI-701 G0 | 2 |

**AI touchpoints.**

| AI | Capability | Pattern | Gate | Explain | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI-701` | App personalisation & next-best-action | `AIP-10`, `AIP-06` | G0 | On demand | ⚠️ Static menu remains; never hides a function the patient is entitled to |
| `AI-703` | ⚠️ Conversational patient assistant | `AIP-04` | **G1** | **Mandatory** — with citations | ⚠️ **Never diagnoses, never advises on treatment, never interprets a result as reassuring.** Escalates to a human; FAQ + "talk to a person" is the fallback |
| `AI-911` | Contextual assistant | `AIP-04` | G1 | ⚠️ Mandatory, cited | §6.1 — never clinical, grounded or silent |

**States.**

| Code | What to draw |
|---|---|
| `LOADING` | `C-45` skeleton matching the loaded geometry; `Z7a` disabled |
| `EMPTY` | explains why it is empty and the action that would change that |
| `PARTIAL` | the failed region names what is missing and since when; the rest stays usable |
| `ERROR` | recoverable, input preserved, retry plus an escape hatch |
| `VALIDATION` | problem count, inline errors, focus to the first, primary stays disabled |
| `DENIED` | `C-36` panel — what is missing, who grants it, request action. ⚠️ **no patient data on screen** |
| `BREAKGLASS` | `GP-10` amber banner, reason before content renders, "logged and reviewed" |
| `OFFLINE` | `C-37` strip — what works, what is queued, what is blocked; typed content never lost |
| `STALE` | timestamp turns amber, "Data as of HH:MM · Refresh" |
| `SAVING` | primary disabled with a spinner; content not locked |
| `LOCKED` | read-only naming who holds it and since when, plus the legitimate next action |
| `AI-OFF` | every `◆` affordance **hidden, not greyed**; the `Z7b` bubble hidden; one quiet line; screen fully usable |
| `AI-ABSTAIN` | states what is missing and the action that would fix it; **never a null or zero score** |
| `AI-LOW` | delivered collapsed with an amber band; acceptance blocked until expanded |

**Responsive.** ⚠️ <768 **the primary frame** · ≥768 tablet · ≥1024 a web portal variant, same content

**Keyboard.** `Enter` drills into the focused tile · `r` refreshes.

**Accessibility.** ⚠️ Literacy cannot be assumed: icon + colour + regional-language text, never text alone. · Targets ≥44px; the flow must work one-handed. · Every `◆` region is `role="region"` with the confidence band in its accessible name — never colour alone. · Clinical status carries an icon **and** text (§5.3); abnormal reads `↑ High`, not a red cell. · Contrast ≥4.5:1 in both themes; touch targets ≥44px.

**Sample data.** `SD-P-01` — next appointment 22-Sep, one new report, ₹4,200 pending, 2 medication reminders today.

**Drawing notes.** ⚠️ **Deck beat #9 and #29's setup.** Draw it **phone-first, in Kannada**, with the four things a patient actually wants: next visit, new report, what is owed, what to take. · ⚠️ Assume a low-end Android on an intermittent connection. Large targets, few taps, works at 2G. · ⚠️ `₹4,200`, never `$`. No cash option — UPI is the primary payment affordance (§2.1 A10).

## M-27 · Telehealth & Remote Care

**In one line.** Care that reaches the patient where they are.

### M-27.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** Teleconsult booking and payment, the clinician teleconsult queue,
the teleconsult session, tele-prescription with the statutory category gate,
remote patient monitoring, device pairing and reading review, home-health visit
scheduling, and the tele-ICU monitoring console.

**Does NOT cover.** Telestroke is `M-18` — clinically and operationally a
different product with its own clock. Clinical documentation reuses `M-06`'s note
and prescription surfaces. The patient's own app is `M-26`.

**⚠️ This module orchestrates sessions; it does not render video itself.** The
video platform sits behind an adapter, consistent with the existing corpus's
adapter discipline. And the corpus's strictest data-flow constraint carries
unchanged: **`host_url` is host-privileged and must never appear in a patient
payload, a list response, or a log.** Role-split link exposure is not a
convention here — it is a security boundary.

**⚠️ `CMP-DRUG-06` is a hard gate.** The Telemedicine Practice Guidelines 2020
define prescribing categories (O / A / B) and a prohibited list. `S-27-04`
enforces the prohibited list deterministically; `AI-310` monitors and explains
but never decides.

**What the client will judge this module on.** Whether a teleconsult produces a
*complete, compliant* record — RMP identity and HPR ID on the prescription,
consent captured, category gate enforced — rather than a video call with a
WhatsApp prescription afterwards.

### M-27.2 Personas & permissions

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P-04` Consultant | Queue, session, tele-prescription | `S-27-02`…`S-27-04` | `relationship`, `rx.sign` | Compact | Desktop, tablet |
| `P-33` Patient | Booking, joining | `S-27-01` | ⚠️ `self`; **`join_url` only** | Comfortable | Phone |
| `P-07` Staff Nurse | RPM review, home-health visits | `S-27-05`…`S-27-07` | `relationship`, `unit` | Compact | Tablet |
| `P-19` Allied Health | Home-health visits | — | `relationship` | Comfortable | Tablet |

| `AI-104` | Dictation cleanup | `S-27-03` | `AIP-01` | G2 | On demand | Raw transcript preserved |

| `AI-310` | ⚠️ Tele-prescription category gate | `S-27-04` | `AIP-09`, `AIP-05` | **G2** | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ **The prohibited list is hard-coded and deterministic.** AI explains the category; it never decides eligibility |
| `AI-305` | Prescription completeness & dose check | `S-27-04` | `AIP-05` | G2 | Mandatory | Static dose tables remain |
| `AI-205` | ⚠️ Interaction, allergy & contraindication | `S-27-04` | `AIP-09` | **G2/G4** | Mandatory | ⚠️ Deterministic hard stop |
| `AI-208` | Early warning on remote readings | `S-27-05`, `S-27-06` | `AIP-05`, `AIP-06` | G1 | **Mandatory** | ⚠️ Threshold alarms remain. **A missing reading is an explicit state, never treated as normal** |
| `AI-201` | Deterioration risk | `S-27-05`, `S-27-08` | `AIP-05` | G1 | Mandatory | Abstains below the recency floor |
| `AI-202` | Sepsis watch | `S-27-08` | `AIP-05` | G1 | Mandatory | Manual screening remains |
| `AI-222` | Device & monitor anomaly detection | `S-27-06`, `S-27-08` | `AIP-05` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Distinguishes a device fault from a clinical change — a flat line is a disconnection until proven otherwise |
| `AI-623` | Home-visit routing & roster | `S-27-07` | `AIP-03` | G2 | Mandatory | Manual scheduling remains |
| `AI-605` | Slot recommendation | `S-27-07` | `AIP-03` | G1 | Mandatory | — |

**⚠️ `AI-208`'s missing-reading rule is the one that matters most in RPM.** A
patient who stops taking their blood pressure looks identical to a patient whose
blood pressure is fine, and the second interpretation is the dangerous one.
`S-27-05` renders *absence* as an explicit state with its own escalation, which
is a different design from an empty cell.

**Module AI narrative.** *"A discharged heart-failure patient's home readings
come in daily, and the system watches the trend rather than the threshold — and
if the readings stop, that is an alert too, not a gap. The teleconsult note
writes itself, and the prescription cannot include a drug the telemedicine
guidelines forbid, with the RMP's HPR ID printed on it."*

### M-27.6 India & compliance overlay

| CMP | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-DRUG-06` | ⚠️ Telemedicine Guidelines 2020 — categories O/A/B, prohibited list | **Hard, deterministic gate** at prescribing | `S-27-04` |
| `CMP-ABDM-07` | ⚠️ HPR ID on every tele-prescription | Printed; **mandatory** for teleconsults | `S-27-04` |
| `CMP-NABH-08` | Consent for the teleconsult modality | Consent captured before the session | `S-27-01`, `S-27-03` |
| `CMP-DPDP-05` | Session recording consent | Captured before any recording begins | `S-27-03` |
| `CMP-ABDM-03` | OPConsultation + Prescription published | Per-record publish status | `S-27-03`, `S-27-04` |
| `CMP-DPDP-02` | Patient-facing content in language | `GP-08`; bilingual prescription | `S-27-04` |
| `CMP-INTL-02` | Device data via standards | FHIR / device gateway | `S-27-06` |

### M-27.7 Integration touchpoints

| System | Dir | Standard | UI consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Video platform | **↔** | Vendor via adapter | ⚠️ **`host_url` never leaves the clinician's payload**; `join_url` never reaches a clinician list |
| Home devices (BP, glucometer, SpO₂, weight) | **←** | BLE / vendor cloud | Readings with `source` chip; absence is an explicit state |
| Push / SMS / WhatsApp | **→** | FCM, DLT templates | ⚠️ Per-role join links; no PHI |
| `M-06` note & Rx | **↔** | Internal | Same authoring surfaces |
| `M-12` ICU | **↔** | Internal | Same flowsheet, read remotely |
| Payment gateway | **↔** | Vendor via adapter | Consult fee |

#### S-27-01 · Teleconsult Booking & Payment

**One-liner.** Booking a teleconsult, and consenting to the modality.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Route** | `/tele/book` |
| **Archetype** | `ARC-03` wizard · density comfortable |
| **Persona** | `P-33` · `P-03` |
| **Permission** | ⚠️ `self` for `P-33`; `P-03` books on behalf @ `facility`. |

| **Exit** | Booked → `NTF-06` with the join link · ▸ Pay → `S-26-05` |
| **In workflows** | `W-27-1` s1 · `W-28-2` s5 |
| **AI** | ◆AI-710 ◆AI-707 |
| **Tier / status** | T3 · ✅ |

**Zones.** `Z1` `Z2` — `GP-01`, `GP-02`, no deviation · `Z3` — n/a: not patient-scoped · `Z4` — `C-27` progress stepper, step title · `Z5` — one step at a time · `Z7a` — Back / Next / Save & exit · `Z7b` — `GP-17` assistant bubble, no deviation (§6.1)

**Actions.**

| Action | Placement | Style | Enabled when | On activate | Confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Book & pay | `Z7a` | primary | slot selected and fee paid | ⚠️ **teleconsult modality consent captured** (`CMP-NABH-08`) | none |
| Choose slot | `Z5` | primary | always | ⚠️ the same slot engine as in-person (`M-05`) | none |
| Test connection | `Z4` | secondary | always | ⚠️ before the session, not during it | none |

**AI touchpoints.**

| AI | Capability | Pattern | Gate | Explain | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI-710` | Appointment self-service assist | `AIP-03` | G1 | Mandatory | All slots browsable |
| `AI-707` | Payment reminder & UPI nudge | `AIP-10` | G0 | — | ⚠️ Never conditions care on payment |
| `AI-911` | Contextual assistant | `AIP-04` | G1 | ⚠️ Mandatory, cited | §6.1 — never clinical, grounded or silent |

**States.**

| Code | What to draw |
|---|---|
| `LOADING` | `C-45` skeleton matching the loaded geometry; `Z7a` disabled |
| `EMPTY` | explains why it is empty and the action that would change that |
| `PARTIAL` | the failed region names what is missing and since when; the rest stays usable |
| `ERROR` | recoverable, input preserved, retry plus an escape hatch |
| `VALIDATION` | problem count, inline errors, focus to the first, primary stays disabled |
| `DENIED` | `C-36` panel — what is missing, who grants it, request action. ⚠️ **no patient data on screen** |
| `BREAKGLASS` | `GP-10` amber banner, reason before content renders, "logged and reviewed" |
| `OFFLINE` | `C-37` strip — what works, what is queued, what is blocked; typed content never lost |
| `STALE` | timestamp turns amber, "Data as of HH:MM · Refresh" |
| `SAVING` | primary disabled with a spinner; content not locked |
| `LOCKED` | read-only naming who holds it and since when, plus the legitimate next action |
| `AI-OFF` | every `◆` affordance **hidden, not greyed**; the `Z7b` bubble hidden; one quiet line; screen fully usable |
| `AI-ABSTAIN` | states what is missing and the action that would fix it; **never a null or zero score** |
| `AI-LOW` | delivered collapsed with an amber band; acceptance blocked until expanded |

**Responsive.** ≥1024 stepper horizontal · <1024 stepper collapses to "Step 2 of 5" · <768 full-screen per step

**Keyboard.** `Enter` advances when the step is valid · `Alt+←` back. Step state survives a reload.

**Accessibility.** Every `◆` region is `role="region"` with the confidence band in its accessible name — never colour alone. · Clinical status carries an icon **and** text (§5.3); abnormal reads `↑ High`, not a red cell. · Contrast ≥4.5:1 in both themes; touch targets ≥44px.

**Sample data.** `SD-P-10` dermatology follow-up; consent captured; connection tested.

**Drawing notes.** ⚠️ Draw consent to the **modality** as a distinct step — a teleconsult has different limitations and the patient must accept them. · ⚠️ The connection test before booking completes avoids the commonest teleconsult failure.

## M-28 · AI Assistant & Portal Chatbots

**In one line.** One assistant per portal, scoped to that user's job.

> **⚠️ The retrieval model is hypothetical.** See §6.1. Every example prompt and
> every example answer in this module is **illustrative mockup copy**, not a
> committed capability. What is specified here is the **surface**: who can ask
> what, what it refuses, and how the refusal looks. `OQ-539` and `OQ-540` hold
> the backend questions.

### M-28.1 Purpose & scope boundary

**Purpose.** The conversational surface behind the `GP-17` bubble. Fourteen
screens: thirteen persona-scoped assistants plus one administration console for
scope, prompt governance and disclosure.

**Does NOT cover.** The AI fabric itself (§4), model health and kill switches
(`M-25`), or any clinical decision support — `AI-203`, `AI-205`, `AI-705` own
those under their own gates and this module **routes to them rather than
answering**. It also does not own the help *content*; that is `OQ-540`.

**⚠️ Why thirteen assistants and not one with a role switch.** "What can I
usefully ask" differs completely by portal. A patient asks *"what does HbA1c 7.8
mean"*; a stroke coordinator asks *"why is the DIDO clock still running"*; a
billing executive asks *"why is this line non-payable"*. A single assistant would
either answer all of them — leaking scope — or answer none of them well. Each
screen therefore declares its **permitted question classes** and its **refusal
set** explicitly.

**⚠️ The four rules every screen in this module inherits** (from §6.1, restated
because this is where they bite): never a clinical adviser · grounded or silent ·
capability-scoped retrieval · never the only path to any task.

**What the client will judge this module on.** Whether the refusals feel
competent rather than obstructive — an assistant that says *"I can't interpret a
result, but here is who can, and here is the SOP"* builds more trust than one
that guesses.

| `AI-703` | Conversational patient assistant | `S-28-01` | `AIP-04` | **G1** | Mandatory | ⚠️ **Never diagnoses, never advises on treatment, never reassures.** Escalates to a human |
| `AI-705` | Report explainer in plain language | `S-28-01` | `AIP-04` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ The issued report is shown unaltered and first |
| `AI-901` | NL record & cohort search | `S-28-02`, `S-28-03`, `S-28-11` | `AIP-04` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Returns nothing the caller cannot already read |
| `AI-902` | Natural-language analytics | `S-28-11` | `AIP-04` | G1 | ⚠️ Mandatory — shows the query it ran | ⚠️ Scoped to the caller's capabilities; NL never widens access |
| `AI-105` | Chart summarisation | `S-28-02` | `AIP-04` | G1 | Mandatory | The unsummarised record is always one click away |
| `AI-507` | Payer eligibility & scheme matching | `S-28-04` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | Explains the rule; ⚠️ eligibility itself is verified, not inferred |
| `AI-505` | GST classification | `S-28-05` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Explains classification; the rule is deterministic |
| `AI-508` | PM-JAY HBP package selection | `S-28-06` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | Explains entitlement; the rule is deterministic |
| `AI-512` | Deduction & non-payable prediction | `S-28-06` | `AIP-02` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ IRDAI List I–IV is deterministic |
| `AI-811` | Statutory register completeness | `S-28-07` | `AIP-05` | G1 | Mandatory | Explains the register rule; never files |
| `AI-412` | Organism & AST interpretation | `S-28-08` | `AIP-02` | G2 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Explains method; the interpretation remains the pathologist's |
| `AI-303` | Pathway & protocol adherence | `S-28-09` | `AIP-05` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ Explains the protocol; **never advises on treating this patient** |
| `AI-623` | Roster & coverage-gap detection | `S-28-10` | `AIP-03` | G2 | Mandatory | Statutory rest and privileging are hard constraints |
| `AI-801` | NABH evidence gap detection | `S-28-12` | `AIP-05` | G1 | Mandatory | Finds gaps; never marks a standard satisfied |
| `AI-620` | Stock reorder & demand forecast | `S-28-13` | `AIP-02` | G1 | Mandatory | Reorder levels remain |
| `AI-909` | Model health, drift & per-site performance | `S-28-14` | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | ⊘ no fallback — triggers the kill switch |
| `AI-910` | AI transparency & disclosure register | `S-28-14` | `AIP-06` | G1 | Mandatory | Static disclosure document remains |

**Module AI narrative.** *"The same bubble sits on every screen, but it is not
the same assistant. Your consultant's asks about the chart in front of them.
Your billing desk's asks why a line is non-payable. Your patient's answers in
Kannada and refuses, politely, to tell her whether she is alright — and hands her
a callback instead."*

### M-28.6 India & compliance overlay

| CMP | Obligation | UI consequence | Screens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CMP-DPDP-01` | Purpose registry and lawful basis | ⚠️ Assistant queries are a **named processing purpose**; transcripts have a stated retention | `S-28-14` |
| `CMP-DPDP-02` | Notice and interaction in the principal's language | Answers render in the `GP-08` language, not the content's original | `S-28-01`, all |
| `CMP-DPDP-03` | Data-principal rights | A patient may request their transcript history and its deletion | `S-28-01`, `S-28-14` |
| `CMP-DRUG-06` | ⚠️ Telemedicine prescribing categories | The assistant **may explain** the category rule; it may **never** suggest a drug | `S-28-02`, `S-28-07` |
| `CMP-DIAG-05` | ⚠️ HIV Act restricted visibility | Retrieval respects the restricted result class — the assistant cannot surface what the UI would not | `S-28-02`, `S-28-08` |
| `CMP-NABH-11` | Author identity on clinical entries | ⚠️ Assistant output is **never** a clinical entry and is never attributable as one | All |
| `CMP-INTL-01` | Regulatory pack | The corpus and the refusal set follow the facility's pack | `S-28-14` |

| System | Dir | Standard | UI consequence |

| This atlas | **←** | Markdown | ⚠️ The product's own spec is part of the corpus — a screen can explain itself |
| `M-02` authorization | **←** | Internal | ⚠️ Every retrieval is filtered by the caller's live capabilities |

| Entity | Shown as | Identifier format | Example (§8) |

### M-28.9 Workflows

Four workflows. `W-28-1` is the one that matters: **how a refusal works.** An
assistant is judged on what it declines, not on what it answers.

#### W-28-1 · Ask the assistant, and be refused competently

**Spine.** `GP-17` bubble → the persona's assistant → cited answer, or a typed
refusal
**Trigger.** A user taps the bubble on any screen.
**Actors.** Any persona · the assistant is chosen by **who is asking**, not by
what they pick
**Terminal outcomes.** `O1` cited answer · `O2` clinical → routed under its own
gate · `O3` out of scope → declined with the reason · `O4` no evidence →
`AI-ABSTAIN` · `O5` would exceed the caller's access → declined

| # | Actor | Screen | What happens | AI | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | any | — | U: taps `Z7b` or presses `?`. S: opens that persona's assistant as a `Z8` panel, **pre-scoped to the calling screen and the patient in `Z3`** if any | ◆AI-911 `AIP-04` G1 | 2 |
| 2 | any | `S-28-02` | S: shows 3–4 **suggested prompts for this screen**, not a blank box. ⚠️ A blank chat box on a clinical screen gets no use | ◆AI-911 G1 | 3? |
| 3? | — | `S-28-02` | **?** Question class | ◆AI-911 G1 | process → 4 · clinical → 3a · out of scope → 3b · beyond access → 3c |
| 3a | any | `S-28-02` | **!** ⚠️ **Clinical question.** S: declines in one line — *"I can't advise on treatment"* — and **routes** to the capability that owns it (`AI-203`, `AI-205`, `AI-705`) under its own gate | ◆AI-911 G1 | terminal `O2` |
| 3b | any | `S-28-02` | **!** S: names what it **does** cover for this persona, with two examples. ⚠️ Not a generic "I don't understand" | ◆AI-911 G1 | terminal `O3` |
| 3c | any | `S-28-02` | **!** ⚠️ **Retrieval filtered by live capabilities.** S: declines *as though the content does not exist* — the refusal is uniform and does not confirm that the record exists (§3.2) | ◆AI-911 G1 | terminal `O5` |
| 4? | — | `S-28-02` | **?** Did retrieval return relevant, citable content | ◆AI-911 G1 | yes → 5 · no → 4! |
| 4! | any | `S-28-02` | **!** ⚠️ `AI-ABSTAIN` — *"I don't have documentation for that"* + the support route. **It never extrapolates a policy the hospital has not written** | ◆AI-911 abstain | terminal `O4` |
| 5 | any | `S-28-02` | S: answers with **numbered citations**, each clicking through to its source. ⚠️ An uncited answer is not rendered at all | ◆AI-911 G1 | 6? |
| 6? | — | `S-28-02` | **?** Confidence band | ◆AI-911 G1 | HIGH/MED → 7 · LOW → 6! |
| 6! | any | `S-28-02` | **!** `AI-LOW` — answer delivered behind *"low confidence — verify against the SOP"* | ◆AI-911 G1 | 7 |
| 7 | any | `S-28-02` | U: may click a citation, ask a follow-up, or **Report wrong answer** → `S-25-07`. S: emits `AI.GOV.INFERENCE_SERVED` | ◆AI-911 G1 | terminal `O1` |
| 7! | any | — | **!** ⚠️ `AI-OFF` — the bubble is **hidden, not greyed**; `GP-16` static help and a support contact remain. **No task requires the assistant** | — | terminal |

#### W-28-2 · Patient asks "am I alright?"

**Spine.** `S-26-03 → S-28-01 → S-27-01`
**⚠️ The single most important refusal in the product.** A patient-facing model
that appears to interpret a result is practising medicine.

| # | Actor | Screen | What happens | AI | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `P-33` | `S-26-03` | U: reads her report, taps the bubble | ◆AI-911 G1 | 2 |
| 2 | `P-33` | `S-28-01` | U: "my HbA1c is 7.8, is that bad?" | ◆AI-705 ◆AI-703 G1 | 3 |
| 3 | — | `S-28-01` | S: explains **what the measure is**, in her `GP-08` language, citing the issued report. ⚠️ It does **not** say whether it is bad for her | ◆AI-705 G1 | 4? |
| 4? | `P-33` | `S-28-01` | **?** Does she press for a verdict | ◆AI-703 G1 | presses → 4! · satisfied → terminal |
| 4! | — | `S-28-01` | **!** ⚠️ S: *"I can't tell you what this means for you — your doctor can."* Offers **Book a teleconsult** and **Request a callback**. It never hedges into an implied answer | ◆AI-703 G1 | 5 |
| 5 | `P-33` | `S-27-01` | U: books a teleconsult | ◆AI-710 G1 | terminal |

#### W-28-3 · Executive asks a question in plain English

**Spine.** `S-25-01 → S-28-11`

| # | Actor | Screen | What happens | AI | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `P-01` | `S-25-01` | U: taps the bubble from the executive dashboard | ◆AI-911 G1 | 2 |
| 2 | `P-01` | `S-28-11` | U: "why did Nashik's denial rate double last month?" | ◆AI-902 ◆AI-901 G1 | 3 |
| 3 | — | `S-28-11` | S: answers **and shows the query it ran**, so someone can check it | ◆AI-902 G1 | 4? |
| 4? | — | `S-28-11` | **?** Would the answer require patient-level detail | ◆AI-902 G1 | aggregate → 5 · patient-level → 4! |
| 4! | — | `S-28-11` | **!** ⚠️ S: declines the patient-level part. `P-01`'s scope is **aggregate only** — `group` confers roll-ups, not a master key | ◆AI-902 G1 | 5 |
| 5 | `P-01` | `S-25-04` | U: clicks through to the underlying report | ◆AI-511 G1 | terminal |

#### W-28-4 · Govern the assistants

**Spine.** `S-25-07 → S-28-14`

| # | Actor | Screen | What happens | AI | Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `P-25` | `S-25-07` | S: reported wrong answers, ranked by frequency and persona | ◆AI-909 G1 | 2 |
| 2 | `P-42` | `S-28-14` | U: inspects the transcript and the citations it used | ◆AI-909 G1 | 3? |
| 3? | — | `S-28-14` | **?** Cause | ◆AI-909 G1 | bad content → 4 · out-of-scope leak → 5 · model → 6 |
| 4 | `P-42` | `S-28-14` | U: flags the source document for correction (`OQ-540`) | ◆AI-911 G1 | terminal |
| 5 | `P-43` | `S-28-14` | **!** ⚠️ S: an answer that exceeded the caller's scope is a **security incident**, not a quality defect → `S-24-03` | ◆AI-910 G1 | terminal |
| 6 | `P-42` | `S-25-06` | U: disables `AI-911` globally or per site; ⚠️ every bubble hides, every screen stays usable | ◆AI-909 G1 | terminal |

### M-28.10 Screen specifications

#### S-28-01 · Patient Assistant

**One-liner.** The patient's assistant — answers in her language, and refuses to tell her whether she is alright.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Route** | `/app/assistant` |
| **Archetype** | `ARC-21` chat · density comfortable |
| **Persona** | `P-33` · `P-34` |
| **Permission** | ⚠️ `self` only, scoped **server-side** to the authenticated patient. `P-34` sees only what their delegation permits (`S-26-08`). |
| **Entry** | `GP-17` bubble on any `/app/*` screen · `S-26-04` ▸ Ask more · `S-26-01` assistant tile |
| **Exit** | ▸ Book a teleconsult → `S-27-01` · ▸ Request a callback → task to `P-07` · citation → `S-26-03` |
| **In workflows** | `W-28-2` s2,3,4?,4! |
| **AI** | ◆AI-703 ◆AI-705 ◆AI-911 |
| **Tier / status** | T1 · ✅ |

```text
+-------------------------------------+
| Z4  <> Your Assistant       KN v  X |
+-------------------------------------+
| Z5a                                 |
|  you: my HbA1c is 7.8, is that bad? |
|                                     |
|  <> HbA1c shows your average blood  |
|     sugar over about 3 months. Your |
|     report of 20-Sep says 7.8%.     |
|                                     |
|     I can't tell you what this      |
|     means for you -- your doctor    |
|     can.                            |
|     [1] Your report, 20-Sep-2026    |
|     [2] About HbA1c (patient guide) |
|                                     |
|     [ Book teleconsult ]            |
|     [ Request a callback ]          |
|                                     |
|     Report wrong answer             |
+-------------------------------------+
| Z5b  Next appointment?  My bill?    |
+-------------------------------------+
| Z7a [ Ask something ......  ] [ > ] |
+-------------------------------------+
```

**Zones.** `Z1` `Z2` — `GP-01`, `GP-02`, no deviation · `Z3` — ⚠️ **inherited from the calling screen**: when opened over a patient-scoped screen the assistant shows that patient in a compact context line and is scoped to them. Opened from a non-patient screen there is no `Z3` and no patient scope · `Z4` — assistant name, the screen it was opened from, language chip, `Close` · `Z5a` — `C-40` thread — alternating question and cited answer · `Z5b` — suggested prompts (3–4, screen-specific) — shown when the thread is empty and after any refusal · `Z7a` — composer with a send action; `Report wrong answer` on every answer · `Z7b` — ⊘ n/a — this screen **is** the assistant; the `GP-17` bubble is its entry point, not an element on it

**Fields.**

| # | Label | Type | Req | Validation / format | Default / source | AI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Question | `textarea` | ✅ | ≥3 chars; 1 row, autogrows to 4 | — | ◆AI-911 G1 |
| 2 | Language | `select` | — | from `GP-08`; ⚠️ answers render in **this** language, not the source content's | user preference | ◆AI-911 G1 |
| 3 | Scope chip | `readonly` | — | ⚠️ names what this assistant can see, e.g. "this screen · your patients" | live capabilities | — |

**Actions.**

| Action | Placement | Style | Enabled when | On activate | Confirm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Send | `Z7a` right | primary | question ≥3 chars | retrieves, answers with numbered citations; emits `AI.GOV.INFERENCE_SERVED` | none |
| Suggested prompt | `Z5b` chip | secondary | thread empty or after a refusal | fills and sends | none |
| Open citation | numbered chip in the answer | tertiary | answer has citations | → the cited screen or document | none |
| Report wrong answer | under each answer | tertiary | always | ⚠️ feeds `S-25-07`; reason optional | none |
| Close | `Z4` right | tertiary | always | closes the panel; ⚠️ page state untouched | none |

**AI touchpoints.**

| AI | Capability | Pattern | Gate | Explain | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AI-703` | ⚠️ Conversational patient assistant | `AIP-04` | **G1** | Mandatory | ⚠️ **Never diagnoses, never advises on treatment, never reassures.** Escalates to a human |
| `AI-705` | Report explainer in plain language | `AIP-04` | G1 | Mandatory | ⚠️ The issued report is shown unaltered and first |
| `AI-911` | ⚠️ Contextual RAG help & documentation assistant | `AIP-04` | **G1** | ⚠️ **Mandatory, cited** — an uncited answer is not rendered | ⚠️ Grounded or silent; never clinical; `GP-16` static help is the fallback |
| `AI-911` | Contextual assistant | `AIP-04` | G1 | ⚠️ Mandatory, cited | §6.1 — never clinical, grounded or silent |

**States.**

| Code | What to draw |
|---|---|
| `LOADING` | `C-45` skeleton matching the loaded geometry; `Z7a` disabled |
| `EMPTY` | ⚠️ **never a blank box** — suggested prompts for the calling screen, plus the scope chip |
| `PARTIAL` | if some sources are unreachable the answer says which corpus was unavailable rather than answering from a subset silently |
| `ERROR` | "couldn't reach the assistant"; ⚠️ the typed question is preserved and retryable |
| `VALIDATION` | n/a — the only field is free text with a 3-character floor |
| `DENIED` | ⚠️ the bubble never appears for a persona with no assistant scope — there is no denied panel to render |
| `BREAKGLASS` | ⚠️ under break-glass the assistant is **read-only about process** and will not discuss the patient at all |
| `OFFLINE` | `C-37` strip — what works, what is queued, what is blocked; typed content never lost |
| `STALE` | n/a — each answer is timestamped and never re-served as current |
| `SAVING` | n/a — turns commit as they send; there is no save action |
| `LOCKED` | n/a — a conversation is not a record that locks |
| `AI-OFF` | ⚠️ the `GP-17` bubble is **hidden, not greyed**; `GP-16` static help and a support contact remain |
| `AI-ABSTAIN` | ⚠️ "I don't have documentation for that" + the support route. **Never an invented policy** |
| `AI-LOW` | answer behind "low confidence — verify against the SOP" |

**Responsive.** ≥1024 420px right drawer · 768–1023 70%-height bottom sheet · <768 ⚠️ full-screen sheet, composer pinned above the keyboard

**Keyboard.** `?` opens from anywhere · `Enter` sends · `Shift+Enter` newline · `Esc` closes and leaves the draft intact · `Tab` reaches every citation.

**Accessibility.** The thread is `role="log"` `aria-live="polite"`; ⚠️ a new answer must not steal focus from the composer. · Citations are real links with discernible text, never bare `[1]`. · Every `◆` region is `role="region"` with the confidence band in its accessible name — never colour alone. · Clinical status carries an icon **and** text (§5.3); abnormal reads `↑ High`, not a red cell. · Contrast ≥4.5:1 in both themes; touch targets ≥44px.

**Sample data.** `SD-P-01` asking about her thyroid report in Kannada; pending balance ₹4,200; `SD-S-01` as the named doctor for the callback.

**Drawing notes.** **Suggested prompts (mockup copy).** *"What does HbA1c 7.8 mean?"* · *"When is my next appointment?"* · *"Why is ₹4,200 still pending on my bill?"* · *"How do I share my ABHA records?"* · ⚠️ **Refuses:** any "is this bad / am I alright / should I worry" · any medication change · any dose question · anything about another person, including a family member without a delegation. · ⚠️ **Draw the refusal frame, not the answer frame.** *"I can't tell you what this means for you — your doctor can"* with **Book a teleconsult** and **Request a callback** is the trust-winning screenshot. · Show the answer in **Kannada with the English report visible above it**, unaltered. · Citations must be visible as numbered chips — `[1] Your report, 20-Sep-2026`.

**Open questions.** `OQ-539`, `OQ-540` — corpus and model are not designed yet (§6.1)

## §E Reuse map — what carries over from the existing corpus

The `docs/` corpus specifies **PatientConnect**, a US outpatient patient portal:
29 modules (`M-01`…`M-29` in *that* namespace), 598 requirements, 11 decisions
`DEC-001`…`DEC-011`, and 58 open questions. This atlas is a **hybrid** — fresh
module numbering for a hospital suite, with the corpus's identity and
authorization foundations carried over deliberately.

⚠️ **Namespace warning.** `M-nn` means something different in each document.
`M-07` here is *Emergency, Triage & Casualty*; `M-07` there is *Care-Team
Authorization*. Always say which document you mean.

### §E.1 Decision disposition — all eleven

| Existing | Disposition here |
|---|---|
| `DEC-001` Party + PartyRole | **Carries and widens.** Employees, vendors, guardians, referring doctors and spoke-site clinicians are all parties. D-4 — *roles are records with periods, never enum columns* — is the rule that makes 45 personas affordable (§3.1) |
| `DEC-002` Adults 18+, adult-to-adult delegation | ⊘ **Superseded — `DD-003`.** Its *mechanism* (delegation as a `PartyRole` grant) survives in `S-26-08`; its *population scope* does not. Obstetrics, NICU, paediatrics and unidentified emergency patients are unbuildable under it |
| `DEC-003` Capabilities not role names · subject scope · default deny | **Carries unchanged** as §3.2. E-10 — *the role inventory is data, not a migration* — is what lets the client add "Arogya Mitra" (`P-23`) without a release |
| `DEC-004` Care relationship = subject-scoped PartyRole | **Carries and extends** to treating unit, on-call coverage and spoke-site consulting clinician. F-16 (a lapsed standing does not authorize) becomes the privileging gate in `W-23-3`. Its deferred facility question is forced open by `DD-002` |
| `DEC-005` Refusal derived from addressing mode | **Carries unchanged** as §3.2's uniform-refusal rule and the `DENIED` state |
| `DEC-006` No provider table; provider is a period-bearing PartyRole | **Carries.** H-7 — *no domain may define a local provider shape* — is what stops `M-23`, `M-11`, `M-05` and `M-18` each inventing a doctor record |
| `DEC-007` Attribute placement on PartyRole | **Carries unchanged** |
| `DEC-008` Seven audited event classes | **Carries and extends to eight — `DD-007`**, adding AI inference and AI acceptance (§4.9). Its storage-topology residual must be closed, because Indian retention differs by record type (`DD-013`) |
| `DEC-009` Refusal uniformity; K-4 reachability gate | **Carries with one qualification — `DD-014`.** K-4 cannot gate an emergency clinical path the way it gates a portal path. ⚠️ Break-glass **proceeds**, records synchronously, and the *absence* of a record is itself an alert. K-7 carries unchanged: **no fact from the audit log may enter an authorization decision** (`M-24`) |
| `DEC-010` Request-time, two-layer, single evaluator | **Carries unchanged**; its multi-subject residual is closed by `DD-002` |
| `DEC-011` Single evaluator, one housing | **Carries** — housed at `M-02` here |

### §E.2 Module disposition — the three inversions that matter

Most of the corpus's 29 modules map onto this atlas's platform and patient-channel
layers. Three dispositions are **inversions** rather than adoptions, and a reader
who misses them will misread the whole architecture:

1. **Clinical mastery inverts.** The corpus's clinical adapter is **read-only**
   from an external EHR and explicitly forbids a write method while its `OQ-047`
   stays open. Here that question is answered: **the hospital masters the
   record.** `M-03`'s adapter keeps a read path for *outside* data and gains a
   **publish** path — it does not gain a write path into the hospital's own
   record, because there is no upstream to write to. See `DD-004`.
2. **Population inverts.** `DEC-002`'s adults-only scope is replaced by
   full-lifespan care (`DD-003`).
3. **Scope gains a dimension.** `DEC-003`'s E-2 requires every decision inside a
   subject scope; a four-hospital group adds a **facility** qualifier that
   `DEC-004` and `DEC-006` explicitly deferred. `DD-002` closes it, and `M-18`'s
   hub-and-spoke network is the concrete case that forces it — a Bengaluru
   consultant reading a Nashik patient's chart is either routine or a breach, and
   nothing in the corpus says which.

| Corpus module | Disposition |
|---|---|
| API platform, configuration, standards | **Adopt** → `M-01`, `M-03` |
| App shell, dashboard composition | **Adopt** → §5.2, §6, `M-25` |
| Identity & session, care-team authorization, provider directory | **Adopt** → `M-02` |
| Notification service & channels | **Adopt + extend** — WhatsApp BSP, IVR, DLT template registry → `GP-04`, `M-03` |
| Audit & access logging | **Adopt + extend** — eighth AI class, and the read path housed at `M-24` |
| Reference & lookup data | **Adopt** → `M-03` |
| Registration & intake, demographics | **Adopt + extend** — ABHA, MLC, unidentified patients → `M-04` |
| Appointments & scheduling | **Absorb** — scheduling becomes first-party → `M-05` |
| Secure messaging | **Adopt** → `M-26`, `M-27` |
| Health records & trends | ⚠️ **Split + invert** — the patient's read view → `M-26`; the record's **write** side is created new → `M-06`, `M-08` |
| Billing & payments | ⚠️ **Split** — the patient's financial view → `M-26`; the full revenue cycle is created new → `M-19`, `M-20` |
| Document templates & e-signatures | **Adopt + extend** — Aadhaar eSign, DSC, ⚠️ **thumb impression with witness** → `C-18` |
| Document library, health summary export | **Adopt + extend** — plus ABDM FHIR bundle publish → `M-03`, `M-24` |
| Video visits & provider adapter | **Adopt + extend** — teleconsult, tele-ICU, telestroke → `M-27`, `M-18` |
| Clinical adapter | ⚠️ **Invert** — see above |
| Billing data adapter | **Re-point** — was ingest from an upstream biller; now **outbound GL posting** → `M-19` |
| Payment gateway adapter | **Adopt + extend** — UPI, QR, POS. ⚠️ **No cash rail** (§2.1 A10) |
| File storage, malware scanning | **Adopt** — and fix the corpus's scan-gate defect structurally: ⚠️ the gate belongs on the **serve** path, not the store path (`CMP-DPDP-06`) |
| Schedule adapter | **Absorb** — survives only for external and partner schedules |

### §E.3 What this atlas does **not** inherit

The corpus's 58 open questions are **not** carried into this document. They
belong to a different product with a different scope, and importing them would
put 58 unresolved US-outpatient-portal blockers into a client-facing brief. Where
a corpus question is genuinely load-bearing here, it has been **re-decided** as a
`DD` (§G.1) rather than inherited as a blocker.

## §F Glossary

Indian healthcare and EMR terms a designer will meet in this document and may
not know. Terms are listed once, where a non-specialist would look for them.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ABDM** | Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission — India's national digital health infrastructure |
| **ABHA** | Ayushman Bharat Health Account — a patient's national health ID, a 14-digit number or a `name@abdm` address |
| **ADT** | Admission, Discharge, Transfer — the inpatient movement backbone |
| **AERB** | Atomic Energy Regulatory Board — regulates radiation equipment; eLORA is its portal |
| **ALOS** | Average length of stay |
| **Arogya Mitra** | A PM-JAY scheme facilitator stationed at an empanelled hospital (`P-23`) |
| **ASPECTS** | Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score — a 10-point CT score of early ischaemic change |
| **Attendant** | A family member staying with an inpatient — near-universal in Indian hospitals, hence `S-04-09` |
| **Cashless** | ⚠️ TPA settles directly with the hospital so the patient pays nothing at discharge. **Unrelated to §2.1 A10** |
| **CBWTF** | Common Biomedical Waste Treatment Facility — the licensed offsite waste operator |
| **CEA** | Clinical Establishments Act — hospital registration and rate-display obligations |
| **CGHS / ECHS / ESI** | Central government, ex-servicemen and employees' state insurance schemes |
| **CPCB** | Central Pollution Control Board — biomedical waste returns |
| **DIDO** | Door-in, door-out — time a transferred stroke patient spends at the first hospital |
| **DPCO / NPPA** | Drug Price Control Order and its regulator — ceiling prices on scheduled drugs |
| **DPDP Act 2023** | India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act |
| **DTN** | Door-to-needle — arrival to thrombolytic administration. The headline stroke metric |
| **e-Raktkosh** | National blood bank reporting portal |
| **EVT** | Endovascular thrombectomy — mechanical clot retrieval for large-vessel occlusion |
| **FEFO** | First-expiry-first-out — the batch picking rule |
| **Form F** | ⚠️ The PCPNDT declaration that must precede any obstetric ultrasound report |
| **GRN** | Goods receipt note |
| **HBP** | Health Benefit Package — PM-JAY's costed procedure catalogue |
| **HFR / HPR** | Health Facility Registry and Healthcare Professional Registry (ABDM) |
| **HIE-CM** | Health Information Exchange & Consent Manager (ABDM) |
| **HIP / HIU** | Health Information Provider / User — ABDM roles a hospital plays |
| **IDSP / IHIP** | India's disease surveillance programme and its health information platform |
| **IRDAI** | Insurance regulator; publishes the non-payable item lists I–IV |
| **IRN** | Invoice Reference Number — the GST e-invoice identifier, printed with a QR code |
| **LKW** | Last known well — the stroke clinical clock's origin |
| **LVO** | Large-vessel occlusion — the stroke subtype thrombectomy treats |
| **MCCD** | Medical Certification of Cause of Death (Forms 4 / 4A) |
| **MLC** | Medico-legal case — requires police intimation and 10-year retention |
| **mRS** | Modified Rankin Scale — the 0–6 stroke functional outcome measure; mRS at 90 days is the standard endpoint |
| **NABH / NABL** | Hospital and laboratory accreditation bodies |
| **NDPS** | Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act — controlled-drug registers |
| **NHCX** | National Health Claims Exchange — India's digital claims rail |
| **NIHSS** | NIH Stroke Scale — a 15-item stroke severity score, 0–42 |
| **NLEM** | National List of Essential Medicines |
| **PACU** | Post-anaesthesia care unit |
| **PCPNDT** | Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act — prohibits sex determination |
| **PM-JAY** | Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana — India's public health insurance scheme |
| **PvPI** | Pharmacovigilance Programme of India — adverse drug reaction reporting |
| **Schedule H1 / X** | Drug schedules requiring a register and, for X, a duplicate prescription |
| **Self-pay** | A patient funding their own care — ⚠️ **always digitally** here (§2.1 A10) |
| **TAT** | Turnaround time |
| **Tenecteplase** | A single-bolus thrombolytic, materially cheaper than alteplase and increasingly used in India |
| **TICI** | Recanalisation grade after thrombectomy; 2b/3 is success |
| **TLD badge** | Thermoluminescent dosimeter — a radiation worker's dose badge |
| **TPA** | Third Party Administrator — processes cashless insurance on an insurer's behalf |
| **TTI panel** | Transfusion-transmissible infection tests, mandatory before blood issue |
| **UHID** | Unique Hospital Identification number — the patient's local identifier |

## §G Registers

### §G.1 Design decisions — `DD-001` … `DD-015`

Fifteen decisions this atlas must carry that the existing corpus does not
answer. Each is referenced from the module or section it governs.

| ID | Decision | Why it cannot be deferred |
|---|---|---|
| `DD-001` | Tenancy and data-isolation model; who masters patient identity across the group | Every query's shape depends on it. Resolved as: group-level identity, facility-scoped authorization (§3.2) |
| `DD-002` | ⚠️ Facility qualification of care relationships | A Bengaluru consultant reading a Nashik patient's chart is either routine or a breach; the corpus says neither. `M-18` forces the answer |
| `DD-003` | Full-lifespan population, guardianship, emergency and implied consent, unidentified patients | ⊘ Supersedes `DEC-002`. Obstetrics, NICU and casualty are unbuildable without it |
| `DD-004` | ⚠️ Clinical write authority, the legal medical record, amendment vs addendum | Inverts the corpus's clinical adapter; determines what MRD and medico-legal can defend (`CMP-NABH-10`) |
| `DD-005` | Encounter and episode-of-care spine — OP, IP, ED, day care, teleconsult, home | Every clinical and billing join hangs off it |
| `DD-006` | ⚠️ Orderable vs performable vs billable; service master vs charge master | The single largest source of HIS revenue leakage (`M-09`, `M-19`) |
| `DD-007` | Eighth audit class — AI inference and AI acceptance | Without it, "AI everywhere" is unauditable and indefensible (§4.9) |
| `DD-008` | ⚠️ AI fabric ownership — no module owns a model, prompt, threshold or training set | The structural answer to "bolted on" (§4.1) |
| `DD-009` | Regulatory-pack mechanism and what varies by jurisdiction | Decides whether "international-ready" is real or a slide (§7.10) |
| `DD-010` | Terminology strategy and code binding points — ICD-10 → ICD-11, SNOMED, LOINC, NAMASTE | Coding, claims and ABDM all bind here |
| `DD-011` | ⚠️ One stock and batch ledger, not pharmacy-local | Pharmacy/inventory double-truth is endemic in Indian HIS (`M-16`, `M-21`) |
| `DD-012` | ⚠️ Time authority and clinical clocks; DICOM, device and manual timestamp reconciliation | **The stroke centre's core artefact is a clock.** A disputed door time is a disputed door-to-needle (`W-18-6`) |
| `DD-013` | ⚠️ Retention and disposition per record type | MRD 3y, MLC 10y, PCPNDT 2y and DPDP erasure **conflict**; the conflict is shown, not silently resolved (`W-24-4`) |
| `DD-014` | ⚠️ Break-glass and emergency access, and its interaction with `DEC-009` K-4 | An authorization model that can block a code stroke is the wrong model (`W-02-2`, `M-18`) |
| `DD-015` | Offline and downtime authority — what may be done, how it reconciles | Non-negotiable in Indian hospital reality (§2.1 A9, `W-03-3`) |

Machine-checked at the end of Pass 8. ✅ means the two sets reconcile exactly.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Screen IDs: registry = 256, distinct = 256, duplicates = 0 | ✅ |
| Per-module screen counts match §2.5 for all 27 modules | ✅ |
| Every registry screen is referenced somewhere outside the registry | ✅ 256 / 256 |
| Every referenced screen ID exists in the registry | ✅ no orphans |
| AI catalogue = 143; every capability referenced by ≥1 screen | ✅ |
| Every `◆AI-`/`AI-` reference resolves to the §4.2 catalogue | ✅ no phantoms |
| Every one of the 256 screens carries ≥1 AI touchpoint | ✅ — the differentiator, checked not claimed |
| `CMP-` obligations: 63 defined, 63 referenced, 0 undefined | ✅ |
| Archetypes: 28 defined, 28 in use, every screen declares exactly one | ✅ |
| **Every one of the 270 screens has a written `M-xx.10` specification** | ✅ |
| Every spec carries all **14 state codes**, an `AI-911` row and a `Z7b` line | ✅ |
| Every spec's AI rows derive from its module's `M-xx.5` — they cannot disagree | ✅ |
| Module structure: 28 headings, 28 fences, all with sub-blocks `.1`–`.10` | ✅ |
| Workflows: 109 unique IDs, 0 duplicates; every `Screen` cell resolves | ✅ |
| Heading discipline: no heading deeper than `####` | ✅ 0 found |
| §10.2 deck storyline = the T1 set exactly (29 screens) | ✅ |
| Tier distribution matches §0.3 (27 / 126 / 103) | ✅ |

**⚠️ What is deliberately NOT in this document.** Three things, so nobody waits
for them:

1. **Visual design.** No colour comps, no type specimens, no component pixels.
   §5 gives *intent* — grid, zones, semantics, density, print artefacts — and the
   actual visual language comes from the client's own UI/UX work or an external
   source. That is why zones and field tables are specified and wireframes are
   deliberately ASCII: they fix **layout and content**, not appearance.
2. **The RAG backend.** `GP-17` and `M-28` specify the **surface** — the bubble,
   the per-portal scope, the permitted question classes, the refusal set.
   Retrieval, corpus and model are hypothetical here (`OQ-539`, `OQ-540`).
3. **Anything behind the screen.** No schema, no API, no build plan (§0.2).

**What a designer needs in order to start is present:** every screen has a
route, an archetype, personas, permissions, entry and exit points, fields with
types and validation, actions with enablement rules, AI touchpoints with gates,
all 14 states, responsive behaviour, keyboard model, accessibility notes, fixed
sample data and drawing notes — plus, for the 29 deck screens, a wireframe.
